jobs.title: Chief, Division of Plastic Surgery, Associate or Full Professor of Surgery at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania
jobs.description:
The Department of Surgery at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for an Associate or Full Professor position in either the non-tenure clinician educator track or the tenure track. Expertise is required in the specific area of plastic surgery. Applicants must have an M.D. degree. Fellowship training in plastic surgery is preferred. They must also be certified by the American Board of Surgery.
  
  
Teaching responsibilities may include education of medical students, residents and fellows.
  
  
Clinical responsibilities may include outpatient, inpatient, and operative care of patients.
  
  
Research or scholarship responsibilities may include clinical or basic science research.
  
  
The successful candidate will have an established clinical reputation, record of academic achievement, and a commitment to mentoring junior faculty.
  
  
This position will be full-time and based primarily at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. It will include the role Chief of the Division of Plastic Surgery, with administrative responsibilities as one of 11 division chiefs in the department. Candidates for the position should embrace all parts of our tripartite mission: to be a world leader in clinical care, research and education. They should have a demonstrated record of excellence in one or more components of that mission and are expected to have a record of service and administration, outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, and a compelling vision for the department and the discipline. Rank will be commensurate with experience.
  
  
Penn Medicine’s Division of Plastic Surgery provides comprehensive care across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and the Philadelphia region, performing more than 4,800 surgeries annually. Clinic locations include the three primary downtown hospitals well as four outlying hospitals. Our Penn Plastic Surgery team specializes in cosmetic and reconstructive surgery, as well as a comprehensive skin care program. We have well-established collaborative reconstruction programs with breast surgery, orthopedics, trauma, sarcoma and soft tissue cancers, and neurosurgery as key partners in this clinical practice. The Division is a national leader and among the world’s largest centers by clinical volume in reconstructive microsurgery. The Division maintains strong partnerships with oncology, trauma and emergency services surgery, imaging, and pathology, enabling a fully integrated care model that supports advanced surgical approaches, coordinated treatment planning, and access to clinical trials.
  
  
As Penn Medicine continues to further align our comprehensive plastic surgery program across its regional network, there is a meaningful opportunity for the Division Chief to provide leadership in the oversight of plastic surgery services to strengthen collaborative programmatic alignment at satellite locations.
  
  
**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**
The University of Pennsylvania is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates are considered for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, creed, national origin (including shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics), citizenship status, age, disability, veteran status or any class protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Professor Term (Open Rank) - Director of Orthopaedic Research
jobs.description:
**Department:**
Orthopedic Surgery
  
  
**Location:**
Health Sciences Center
  
  
**Time Type:**
Full time
  
  
**Worker Type:**
Regular Term (Fixed Term)
  
  
**Job Req ID:**
R109547
  
  
**Position Description:**
This role is for a Director of Orthopaedic Research in the Department of Orthopedic Surgery. It exists to make research usable for busy surgeons. The Director is a full-time term faculty member with an appointment renewed annually. The Director of Orthopaedic Research sits with faculty and residents to turn a clinic idea into an answerable question and a study design. Core staff then write the protocol, file the IRB, collect and analyze the data, and draft the paper. The surgeon shapes the clinical message and presents. The Director also helps the department compete for grants, with faculty as PI.
  
  
Qualifications:
  
  

* Doctoral degree and a substantial peer-reviewed record in musculoskeletal science. Leadership of a multi-investigator portfolio, including IRB oversight, trainee mentorship, study design with clinicians, and supervision of professional staff as a peer with surgical faculty.
* Demonstrated grantsmanship: industry, foundation, or federal proposals in support of faculty PIs. Eligibility for Professor (Term). Preferred: prior orthopaedic faculty appointment at associate professor or above, and national scholarly visibility.

Essential duties:
  
  

* Sit with surgeons and residents to refine the question, test feasibility, and design the study. Run a single intake. Accept, reshape, or decline studies within one week.
* Hold authorship and data standards. No departmental dataset leaves the core without a written agreement. The office is measured on submitted papers and submitted proposals, not on activity.
* Help the department win funding. Identify industry, foundation, and federal mechanisms. Pair faculty with opportunities. Contribute design, methods, and grantsmanship. Faculty remain PI. Route proposals with SOM sponsored programs.
* Hire and supervise core staff, beginning with the clinical research coordinator. Own IRB, HIPAA, and sponsor compliance. Monthly dashboard to the Chair.
* Direct resident research. Place medical students and other learners only on projects that serve department needs. Every resident has a named mentor and a tracked project. Surgeons present.

jobs.title: Tenure Track Nursing Faculty Open Rank – RISE AI
jobs.description:
***Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through the internal application process.***
**Job Category:**
Faculty
  
  
**Employment Type:**
Regular
  
  
**Job Profile:**
Assistant Professor
  
  
**Job Summary:**
This position is part of the Wisconsin Research, Innovation and Scholarly Excellence (RISE) Initiative. Through accelerated and strategic faculty hiring, research infrastructure enhancement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and increased student and educational opportunities, RISE addresses complex societal challenges of importance to the state, nation and world. Building on the University of Wisconsin–Madison’s strengths, RISE expands the University’s successful track record of connecting with communities and industry on collaborative solutions. RISE-AI (Artificial Intelligence) is set to propel the university to a new level of capacity, with a focus on both the core technical dimensions as well as the human-centered implications of artificial intelligence.
  
  
Over three academic years, UW–Madison will substantially increase current hiring levels, bringing nearly 250 new RISE faculty to campus. Candidates hired through RISE will join a community of scholars working across disciplines, schools and colleges on research, teaching and outreach endeavors. The community will engage regularly in venues such as seminar series and colloquia to share ongoing projects and identify opportunities to work together. The University will support the community, facilitating access to research infrastructure, and funding to support broad and rich collaboration.
  
  
Further information regarding RISE can be found at
**:**
https://rise.wisc.edu/.
  
  
The School of Nursing at UW–Madison is seeking productive nurse scientists to join our tenure track faculty as part of the RISE-AI initiative. Successful candidates will join a vibrant and collaborative group of scientists and scholars conducting innovative and impactful research aimed at improving health care services and individual and population health. Our faculty have research partnerships across campus, communities, schools, homes, and at University Hospital (UW Health) next door.
  
  
We seek candidates who will develop and maintain a robust externally funded research program. Qualified applicants will have a program of research on the design, implementation, use and/or evaluation of AI-assisted technologies to address important challenges in health, healthcare, and nursing. Areas of particular interest include:
  
  

* healthcare and nursing workflows and workforce transformation;
* clinical and systems decision-making in nursing;
* improving healthcare quality and safety;
* expanding access to care;
* improving outcomes for patients, caregivers, and communities;
* human-centered, responsible, and equitable implementation of AI in nursing.

Candidates will be encouraged to collaborate with other faculty across campus who join the university as part of the RISE-AI initiative including within the School of Nursing, and the College of Computing & Artificial Intelligence, College of Engineering, College of Letters and Sciences, School of Education, School of Human Ecology, School of Business, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, the Law School, and the School of Medicine and Public Health.
  
  
Successful candidates for these positions will also teach courses aligned with their expertise in Baccalaureate, Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP), and PhD programs, and will mentor undergraduate honors and graduate students in research and scholarship. Service to the school, university, and profession are expectations of tenure track faculty.
  
  
School of Nursing faculty are expected to work onsite with remote work flexibility. It is anticipated that this position requires work to be performed in-person, onsite, at designated campus work locations when necessary or at other locations or using remote work technology as needed or preferred.
  
  
**Key Job Responsibilities:**
RISE faculty will participate in interdisciplinary and collaborative efforts with other departments, schools, and colleges. Tenure-track faculty at the UW–Madison School of Nursing conduct research, teach courses, mentor students, and contribute to school, university, community, and professional activities through academic citizenship, service, and leadership.
  
  
**Research Responsibilities**

* Successful candidates will be expected to develop and maintain a collaborative, innovative, robust, and highly visible research program that entails conceptualizing, designing, and conducting research studies; managing research staff; following all research compliance policies; disseminating research results; and seeking extramural funding. Research programs should be consistent with national priorities for extramural funding.

**Teaching Responsibilities**

* Successful candidates will be expected to teach courses aligned with their expertise at Baccalaureate and/or graduate levels. Teaching may include co-teaching in active learning environments and interprofessional education with health sciences students and faculty. Teaching may include face-to-face, blended, and online delivery.
* Research mentoring of undergraduate honors students, PhD students, and postdoctoral trainees/fellows is expected.

**Service Responsibilities**

* Successful candidates will be expected to actively contribute to school, university, community, and professional committees and other activities through academic service.

**Department:**
For over 100 years, the University of Wisconsin–Madison's School of Nursing has been committed to enhancing healthcare through teaching and research. With a mission to develop nurse leaders, innovators, and advocates for the profession and society through research, education, practice, policy, and outreach; we aim to make discoveries, enhance systems, and advance health and health equity for Wisconsin and beyond.
  
  
The UW–Madison School of Nursing ranks first in Wisconsin and 19th nationally according to U.S. News and World Report. Additionally, UW–Madison ranks among the top eight U.S. public universities and surpasses $1 billion in annual research expenditures. At the heart of UW–Madison is the
**Wisconsin Idea**
(https://www.wisc.edu/wisconsin-idea/)—a guiding principle that education should influence people’s lives beyond the boundaries of the classroom.
  
  
Our home, Signe Skott Cooper Hall, showcases the power, impact, and future of nursing with high fidelity simulation labs, 25 research suites, an active-learning classroom complex, exercise spaces, self-care rooms, and an accessible auditorium. Our School is in the heart of Madison, near Lake Mendota and the Lakeshore Nature Preserve that serves as home to many migratory birds such as sandhill cranes, frequent visitors to our courtyard. Often voted one of the best places to live in the U.S., Madison blends green spaces and urban areas; outdoor recreation and vibrant city life; stimulating cultural offerings and lively festivals.
  
  
From our world-class facilities and research opportunities to our commitment to health equity and culture of wellness, we encourage collaboration, innovation, and growth for everyone at our School.
  
  
As part of the UW–Madison Health Care Component (HCC) and your work at the School of Nursing, you may have access to PHI (personal health information). All School faculty, staff, students, volunteers, and unpaid affiliates are required to complete HIPAA training as part of their orientation.
  
  
Official transcripts will be required upon hire.
  
  
**Compensation:**
Negotiable – 9-month (C-basis) / full-time (100%) / ongoing / renewable
  
  
Actual pay will depend on experience and qualifications. This position offers a comprehensive benefits package, including generous sick leave, competitively priced health/dental/vision/life insurance, tax-advantaged savings accounts, and participation in the nationally recognized Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS) pension fund. For a summary of benefits, please see https://www.wisconsin.edu/ohrwd/benefits/download/fasl.pdf.
  
  
**Required Qualifications:**
Well-qualified applicants must show evidence of the following:
  
  

* Research training or experience in conducting health-related research projects
* Potential for developing an outstanding scholarly research program
* A record of research dissemination through publications and/or presentations
* Potential for securing extramural grant funding
* Knowledge and/or emerging skills to teach and mentor at undergraduate or graduate levels in nursing or health-related field
* Potential for contributions to the outreach and service missions of the School of Nursing
* Ability to work effectively within a diverse community, and commitment to promoting a climate of belonging within our campus and associated communities
* For appointment at the rank of Associate or full Professor, a substantially nationally recognized record of research, publication, teaching, and service meeting UW–Madison and School of Nursing tenure standards is required.

The successful candidate will be required to have or be eligible for Wisconsin RN licensure on or before the first day of employment.
  
  
**Education:**
**Required**

* PhD – earned research doctorate (PhD or equivalent) in Nursing or related field required. If earned research doctorate is not in nursing, a graduate degree in nursing is required.

**How to Apply:**
To begin the application process, click the “Apply” button. A complete application will include the following:
  
  

* Cover letter
* Current curriculum vitae
* Research program statement (2 pages)
* Teaching philosophy statement (1 page)
* One (1) representative data-based peer-reviewed publication

**Important: The application has only one attachment field. Upload the above documents in that field, either as a single combined PDF file or as multiple files in the same upload area. Failure to submit complete application materials may result in ineligibility for consideration for this position. Please submit only the materials specified; additional materials will not be reviewed.**
You will be asked to provide the names and contact information of three (3) references. For those who advance in the process, references will be contacted to provide letters of recommendation. Candidates will be notified prior to contacting references.
  
  
To ensure consideration, complete applications must be received by 11:59pm on November 19, 2026. The position will remain open and applications may be considered until the position is filled.
  
  
**Contact Information:**
Samantha Noordhoek, noordhoek@wisc.edu, (608) 262-0051
  
  
Relay Access (WTRS): 7-1-1: See RELAY\_SERVICE for further information.
  
  
**Institutional Statement on Diversity:**
Diversity is a source of strength, creativity, and innovation for UW-Madison. We value the contributions of each person and respect the profound ways their identity, culture, background, experience, status, abilities, and opinion enrich the university community. We commit ourselves to the pursuit of excellence in teaching, research, outreach, and diversity as inextricably linked goals.
  
  
The University of Wisconsin-Madison fulfills its public mission by creating a welcoming and inclusive community for people from every background - people who as students, faculty, and staff serve Wisconsin and the world.
  
  
**The University of Wisconsin-Madison is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**
Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, including but not limited to, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, pregnancy, disability, or status as a protected veteran and other bases as defined by federal regulations and UW System policies. We promote excellence by acknowledging skills and expertise from all backgrounds and encourage all qualified individuals to apply. For more information regarding applicant and employee rights and to view federal and state required postings, visit the Human Resources Workplace Poster website.
  
  
To request a disability or pregnancy-related accommodation for any step in the hiring process (e.g., application, interview, pre-employment testing, etc.), please contact the Divisional Disability Representative (DDR) in the division you are applying to. Please make your request as soon as possible to help the university respond most effectively to you.
  
  
Employment may require a criminal background check. It may also require your references to answer questions regarding misconduct, including sexual violence and sexual harassment.
  
  
The University of Wisconsin System will not reveal the identities of applicants who request confidentiality in writing, except that the identity of the successful candidate will be released. See Wis. Stat. sec. 19.36(7).
  
  
The Annual Security and Fire Safety Report contains current campus safety and disciplinary policies, crime statistics for the previous 3 calendar years, and on-campus student housing fire safety policies and fire statistics for the previous 3 calendar years. UW-Madison will provide a paper copy upon request; please contact the University of Wisconsin Police Department.

Join the University of Michigan School of Nursing as a clinical track faculty member at the Clinical Assistant Professor or Clinical Associate Professor level. You hold a doctorate in nursing and Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Board Certification (AGACNP-BC or ACNPC-AG). Faculty at RVU CVM will collaborate closely with accomplished peers to design, develop, and continuously refine courses, playing a central role in shaping both the program and the future of veterinary education. You’ll teach, mentor, and innovate in state‑of‑the‑art facilities in beautiful Billings, Montana, where exceptional quality of life, a welcoming community, and unparalleled access to outdoor recreation come together.

$149,864 - $196,539 per year. + Specific interest and background in collaborative research with CVM faculty in other departments is desirable.
+ Develop and contribute to extension and continuing education programs, in collaboration with other departments and/or other schools.

+ Faculty Senate
+ Departmental Meetings (when required)
+ Departmental Faculty evaluations (when required)
+ College/University committees

* DVM and/or PhD from an accredited institution.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Board eligible or board certification.
* Experience and interest in Equine Medicine & Surgery research is highly desired.

jobs.title: Faculty Position in Electrical Engineering
jobs.description:
**Job Description**

The Division of Engineering and Applied Science at the California Institute of Technology invites applications for tenure-track/tenured faculty positions. We seek highly qualified candidates committed to a career in teaching, mentoring and research excellence in the department of Electrical Engineering. Preference will be given to candidates at the Assistant Professor level; however, well-qualified applicants at the associate or full professor level may also be considered. Our department is a unique environment where innovative, interdisciplinary, and foundational research is conducted in a collegial atmosphere.

We are seeking candidates in the broad area of information systems, including decision systems, systems for science, distributed systems, sensory systems (such as speech and vision), signal processing, data science, data communications and storage, energy systems, control, robotics, artificial intelligence, networking, and human-in-the-loop systems. For tenure-track candidates, the initial appointment is contingent upon completion of the Ph.D. degree. It is also anticipated that a successful candidate would collaborate broadly with investigators both within and beyond the Engineering and Applied Science Division, as well as in centers at Caltech including, for example, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the Center for Sensing to Intelligence, the Center for Autonomous Systems and Technologies, the Institute for Quantum Information and Matter, the Chen Institute for Neuroscience, the Merkin Institute, and the Resnick Sustainability Institute.

Applications should be submitted online. Reviewing of applications will begin on November 8, but full consideration will be given to all candidates who apply by **December 6, 2026.**

**General Summary**

Western Michigan University’s College of Education and Human Development invites applications for the position of Assistant Professor of Organizational Change Leadership. The individual in this position will serve in the Organizational Change Leadership (OCL) unit within the Department of Educational Leadership, Research, and Technology at Western Michigan University (WMU). The OCL unit is comprised of a suite of academic programs that includes a PHD in Organizational Change Leadership, an MA in Organizational Change Leadership, a Graduate Certificate in Organizational Change Leadership, and an Undergraduate Minor in Organizational Change Leadership.

We seek to hire someone who can fill needed content expertise areas (organizational development, organizational culture, power and politics, and applied change leadership), and provide new energy and perspectives related to teaching; recruiting, retaining, and advising students; and research. This individual will also serve on committees for doctoral students in the PhD in Organizational Change Leadership. To attain and keep graduate faculty status (which is required to teach in a graduate program at the institution), this individual will be required to maintain an active research agenda. Ideally, this faculty member should have connections with thought leaders in the profession, as well as in professional associations in the field of organizational development and change.

The individual in this position will also be expected to teach courses, maintain office hours, and support program initiatives on campus, in-person in Kalamazoo, Michigan.

  

**Major Duties**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Organizational Change Leadership beginning in August 2027, with primary responsibility for high-quality online instruction.
* Maintain an active research agenda in organizational development and change and contribute meaningfully to the advancement of the field.
* Advise and mentor students across the OCL undergraduate minor, graduate certificate, master’s, and doctoral programs.
* Recruit and engage prospective students and contribute to the continued growth and visibility of the OCL programs.
* Contribute to curriculum innovation, course development, and continuous improvement across OCL programs.
* Contribute actively to the intellectual and professional life of the OCL unit and provide service to the department, college, and university.
* Maintain a visible presence in the organizational development and change scholarly community through conference presentations, publications, professional service, and disciplinary leadership.
* Engage actively in relevant professional associations, particularly the Organization Development and Change (ODC) and Management Consulting (MC) Divisions of the Academy of Management.

  

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Earned doctorate in Organizational Development and Change, Organizational Behavior, Organization Studies, Industrial-Organizational Psychology, Organizational Psychology, Organizational and Social Psychology, or Human and Organizational Studies, with a substantive emphasis on organizational development, conferred by the start of a Fall 2027 appointment from an accredited institution.
* An emerging research agenda and record of peer-reviewed publications and/or presentations appropriate for career stage in organizational development and change, organizational behavior, or organizational studies.
* Demonstrated professional and/or scholarly engagement in organizational development and change through participation in professional associations, conferences, scholarly networks, and/or professional practice.
* Demonstrated experience teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses in one or more of the following areas: organizational development, organizational change, organizational diagnosis, leadership, group dynamics, organizational power and politics, organizational culture, or closely related areas of organizational studies.
* Experience with, or demonstrated ability to develop, high-quality online instruction.
* Commitment to working with a broad range of students and mentoring adult learners from varied professional, organizational, and educational backgrounds.

  

**Desired Qualifications**

* Substantive organizational consulting or change leadership experience across settings such as business and industry, nonprofit organizations, healthcare, government, or the military.
* Demonstrated ability to translate organizational development and change theory and research into professional practice.
* Expertise in quantitative, qualitative, and/or mixed-methods research.
* Experience advising and mentoring undergraduate, master’s, and/or doctoral students, including service on dissertation committees.
* Demonstrated expertise in curriculum development and the design of innovative courses and learning experiences for working professionals.

Located in Georgetown, Texas, Southwestern University is an independent, four-year undergraduate institution offers a top-ranked integrated arts and sciences curriculum that incorporates the humanities, fine arts, social sciences, and natural sciences.

At Southwestern University, we are committed to fostering an environment where every individual feels respected, valued, and empowered. We believe that a thriving community is built on the strength of varying perspectives and experiences, and we strive to create an atmosphere of mutual respect and understanding. Our actions are guided by a commitment to fairness, openness, and the belief that our differences are what make us stronger as a whole.

---------------------

The Department of Art and Art History at Southwestern University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Art (Sculpture) position beginning in August 2027. The successful candidate will have a strong record of professional achievement and a commitment to undergraduate teaching. Applicants should be proficient in wood and metal fabrication, welding, and mold making, while also engaging with alternative practices and expanded approaches to sculpture. Interests in socially engaged practices, material studies, or digital processes are especially welcome. As a liberal arts and sciences university, Southwestern welcomes candidates who bring interdisciplinary approaches to their teaching and scholarship and are eager to collaborate with colleagues across departments and programs.

The successful candidate will teach five courses per academic year. Teaching responsibilities will span introductory through advanced sculpture and include courses in the foundations program. The candidate will also teach interdisciplinary senior seminar and capstone courses as part of the department’s course rotation. The department welcomes opportunities to develop elective courses in the candidate’s areas of specialization as staffing and curriculum allow. Additional responsibilities include maintaining an active studio practice and exhibition record, academic advising, and departmental and university service. * MFA in Sculpture or Studio Art (sculpture emphasis) from an accredited institution

**Description**
The Department of Surgery at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for an Associate or Full Professor position in either the non-tenure clinician educator track or the tenure track. Expertise is required in the specific area of plastic surgery. Applicants must have an M.D. degree. Fellowship training in plastic surgery is preferred. They must also be certified by the American Board of Surgery.
  
  
Teaching responsibilities may include education of medical students, residents and fellows.
  
  
Clinical responsibilities may include outpatient, inpatient, and operative care of patients.
  
  
Research or scholarship responsibilities may include clinical or basic science research.
  
  
The successful candidate will have an established clinical reputation, record of academic achievement, and a commitment to mentoring junior faculty.
  
  
This position will be full-time and based primarily at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. It will include the role Chief of the Division of Plastic Surgery, with administrative responsibilities as one of 11 division chiefs in the department. Candidates for the position should embrace all parts of our tripartite mission: to be a world leader in clinical care, research and education. They should have a demonstrated record of excellence in one or more components of that mission and are expected to have a record of service and administration, outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, and a compelling vision for the department and the discipline. Rank will be commensurate with experience.
  
  
Penn Medicine’s Division of Plastic Surgery provides comprehensive care across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and the Philadelphia region, performing more than 4,800 surgeries annually. Clinic locations include the three primary downtown hospitals well as four outlying hospitals. Our Penn Plastic Surgery team specializes in cosmetic and reconstructive surgery, as well as a comprehensive skin care program. We have well-established collaborative reconstruction programs with breast surgery, orthopedics, trauma, sarcoma and soft tissue cancers, and neurosurgery as key partners in this clinical practice. The Division is a national leader and among the world’s largest centers by clinical volume in reconstructive microsurgery. The Division maintains strong partnerships with oncology, trauma and emergency services surgery, imaging, and pathology, enabling a fully integrated care model that supports advanced surgical approaches, coordinated treatment planning, and access to clinical trials.
  
  
As Penn Medicine continues to further align our comprehensive plastic surgery program across its regional network, there is a meaningful opportunity for the Division Chief to provide leadership in the oversight of plastic surgery services to strengthen collaborative programmatic alignment at satellite locations.

jobs.description:
**UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT URBANA-CHAMPAIGN**
**DEPARTMENT OF VETERINARY CLINICAL MEDICINE**
**Tenure-Track or Clinical Track Open Rank Professor in Small Animal Orthopedic Surgery**
**Full-time, 100% (12-month basis)**
**Requirements:**
The successful candidate must have a DVM degree or equivalent and have achieved American College of Veterinary Surgeons (ACVS) board certification or completed residency training with credentials accepted by the ACVS. Preference will be given to candidates with ACVS certification, advanced degree(s), a track record in scholarship, and/or prior research training.
  
  
**Professional opportunities:**
Our faculty and staff provide broad public engagement through operation of the Veterinary Teaching Hospital, a regional primary and referral care center for the delivery of state-of-the art veterinary medical services. The Department of Veterinary Clinical Medicine features modern animal care and research facilities. Our faculty provide instruction and service and conduct discovery relevant to companion animals; horse, food and fiber animals; and wildlife and zoological species. We are dedicated not only to animal health and welfare, but also to the improved understanding of the human-animal bond, food production systems, and ecosystem health. The University of Illinois is a premier public research university and is gaining recognition for its uniquely multidisciplinary and extremely highly collaborative and welcoming research environment.
  
  
The University of Illinois has a tradition of excellence as a Land Grant University and a Tier One Research University. The College of Veterinary Medicine is lauded for our unique, clinically integrated professional veterinary curriculum that is supported by innovators in teaching, learning, course design, continuing education, and medical illustration as well as a state-of-the-art Clinical Skills Learning Center. The College is also focused on advancing clinical, applied, and translational research efforts across the college and university by developing quality relationships with world-class scientists and investigators. With ready access to these resources, the motivated candidate will find significant opportunity and support to craft a fulfilling and rewarding career.
  
  
**Personal opportunities:**
Urbana-Champaign offers the residential advantages of a medium-sized university city, including a rich experience of farm-to-table cuisine, music, art, all-season outdoor activities, and other life-enriching opportunities. In 2024 Forbes ranked the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign as #13 among all US public colleges, on the basis of return on investment, student success, student debt, and alumni leadership and influence. Only one other campus featuring a veterinary college ranked above U. of I.
  
  
**Duties:**
The University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital is a full-service facility with newly equipped surgical suites and fluoroscopic capabilities. The orthopedic service at the University of Illinois sees a wide variety of orthopedic cases. Equipment to perform arthroscopy, interlocking nail (I-Loc Ò IM Fixator) and total hip replacement are available, in addition to standard orthopedic equipment needed for fracture repair and other commonly seen orthopedic conditions. On-site services include digital radiography, 128 slice computed tomography, 3T MRI, radiation therapy, Dual Energy X-Ray absorptiometry (DEXA), force plate gait analysis, and physical rehabilitation. Percent time dedicated to teaching, scholarly activities, and clinical service will be based on the successful candidate’s appointment title.
  
  
The small animal surgery program at the University of Illinois’ College of Veterinary Medicine is composed of a highly productive and dynamic group of specialists who have achieved excellence in the arenas of comparative research, resident instruction, and high-quality application of cutting-edge diagnostic modalities and therapies for companion animals.
  
  
Upon joining our team, the successful candidate will provide clinical service in small animal orthopedic surgery, contribute to the didactic and clinical instruction of surgical residents, surgical; interns, rotating interns, and veterinary students, and communicate effectively with clients and primary veterinarians. A strong interest and/or experience in joint replacement is welcomed. In addition, we have a well-established and busy rehabilitation therapy program integral to our orthopedic service with opportunities for growth.
  
  
The University of Illinois is highly focused on faculty and service development and growth and will provide significant funding and support for additional equipment and training to candidates with special interests or skills in areas relevant to small animal orthopedic surgery. Teaching responsibilities will include didactic, small group, and laboratory instruction of veterinary and graduate students. The successful applicant will be expected to participate in clinically and scientifically relevant scholarship. Candidates interested in collaborative research will find ample opportunities to partner within our thriving faculty as well as with scientists and investigators on our main campus. Our veterinarians have been integral in the creation of the new Carle-Illinois College of Medicine- the world’s first bioengineering-based college of medicine- leveraging advanced technology to train physician- innovators to deliver better, more compassionate, and accessible care to patients worldwide.
  
  
**Salary:**
The budgeted salary range for this position is $160,000 to $200,000. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including equivalent years in rank, training, and field or discipline; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable positions. The University of Illinois offers a competitive benefits package. A summary explanation of these benefits can be found at https://www.hr.uillinois.edu/benefits . This position is eligible for sponsorship for work authorization, except for sponsorship of a new H1B petition that would incur the $100,000 fee.
  
  
**Starting date:**
As soon as possible after close of position.
  
  
**Application procedures:**
Applicants may be interviewed prior to the closing date; however, no hiring decision will be made until after that date. Applications will continue to be accepted until the position is filled. Please create your candidate profile through https://jobs.illinois.edu/. Candidates are required to upload all application materials, including your letter of interest, resume, transcripts, and names and email contact information for at least three references by November 15, 2026.
  
  
Additional information about the position may be obtained by contacting:
  
  
Heidi Phillips VMD, DACVS-SA
  
  
Chair, Search Committee
  
  
Department of Veterinary Clinical Medicine University of Illinois

philli@illinois.edu

With a land-grant heritage rooted in progress, Illinois faculty drive paradigm-shifting discoveries, mentor future leaders, and collaborate across 15 colleges and instructional units and more than 20 research institutes. The university’s legacy of excellence includes
**24 Nobel Prizes and 29 Pulitzer Prizes**
awarded to its faculty and alumni, $755 million in sponsored research funding, and 94 academic programs ranked in the top 20 nationally. **Next Lives at the University of Cincinnati**
Founded in 1819, the University of Cincinnati ranks among the nation’s best urban public research universities. Home to more than 53,600 students, 12,000 faculty and staff, and over 360,000 living alumni, UC, a Carnegie 1 institution, combines research prowess with a physical setting The New York Times has called “the most ambitious campus design program in the country." UC's momentum has never been stronger as the anchor of the Cincinnati Innovation District, the oldest cooperative education (co-op) program in the country with students earning $94 million annually through paid experiences, an academic health system, and as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The university contributes $10.6 billion in economic impact to the city and $22.7 billion to the state of Ohio. At UC, next is all of us. Learn more at uc.edu.
  
  
UC is a mission-driven organization where we are committed to student success and positively transforming the community through scholarship and service. We thrive on innovation, making an impact, and fostering an environment where staff and faculty are key contributors to UC’s success.
  
  
**Job Overview**
The Department of Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) is pleased to announce a search for a 2027 – 2028 Visiting Assistant Professor in LGBTQ+ Studies. The position will primarily support the department’s online LGBTQ+ Studies Certificate, for which courses are taught in an asynchronous online format. There will also be opportunities for in-person teaching according to the candidate’s interests and department needs. The LGBTQ+ Studies Certificate currently serves undergraduate students, many of whom pursue it as a complement to their major or minors across the college and university.
  
  
The expected teaching load is three courses per semester or the equivalent, with minimal service expectations. Although research productivity is not required or evaluated, visiting faculty are eligible to apply for research and professional development funding from various departmental and college sources. Additional responsibilities include participating in WGSS collegial life such as attending faculty meetings, brown bags, colloquia, and other departmental events.
  
  
This is a 12-month appointment with an intended start date of August 16, 2027. There is a possibility that the position could be renewed for a second year depending on satisfactory performance and funding availability. The selected candidate will be provided with an office in the department and is expected to spend the academic year in residence at UC.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Teach undergraduate courses in the online LGBTQ+ Studies Certificate and related areas within the WGSS curriculum
* Teach in-person undergraduate or graduate courses including large lectures and discussion-based seminars
* Develop and deliver engaging, student-centered instruction
* Prepare syllabi, assignments, and assessments aligned with program outcomes
* Maintain accurate academic records and grading
* Provide timely feedback and support students’ academic growth
* Participate in departmental meetings and appropriate service activities
* Other related duties as assigned, including completion of professional development courses through UC Online.

**Minimum Requirements**

* PhD in feminist studies or related field.
* One semester designing and teaching an online course at the collegiate level.
* One semester teaching in-person at the collegiate level.

**Application Process**

* We will begin reviewing applications on December 7, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.
* Qualified and interested applicants must apply online.
* In addition to the online application, please submit: a cover letter that discusses your expertise in LGBTQ and feminist studies and your specific interest in and approach to online teaching; a curriculum vitae; one sample syllabus for a courses taught online, and teaching evaluations for at least one course.
* Applicants who have not yet completed their Ph.D. must also include a letter from their Committee Chair discussing progress to completion and specifying the date of the dissertation defense.
* Applicants who make the short list will be asked to arrange for two confidential letters of recommendation to be sent to: wgssdepartment@ucmail.uc.edu. Submitted reference letters should put "Letter of recommendation for [applicant's name]" in the message title.
* Preliminary interviews will be held towards the end of January 2027 via Zoom, with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027.
* Visa eligibility: This position is not eligible for H-1B sponsorship. Foreign national scholars will be appointed under J-1 visa during the two-year fellowship.

**Compensation And Benefits**
UC offers an exceptional benefits package designed to support your well-being, financial security, and work-life balance. (UC Benefits) Eligibility may vary by position and FTE status. Highlights include:
  
  
**Comprehensive Tuition Remission**
UC provides tuition remission for you and your eligible dependents, covering tuition costs for nearly all undergraduate and graduate programs offered by the university.
  
  
**Robust Retirement Plans**
As a UC employee, you won’t contribute to Social Security (except Medicare). Instead, you’ll choose between state pension plans (OPERS, STRS) or an Alternative Retirement Plan (ARP), with UC contributing 14–18% of your salary based on position.
  
  
**Real Work-Life Balance**
UC prioritizes work-life balance with a generous time-off policy, including:
  
  
Vacation and sick time
  
  
11 paid holidays and additional end-of-year paid time off (Winter Season Days)
  
  
6 weeks of paid parental leave for new parents
  
  
**Additional Benefits Include**

* Competitive salary based on experience
* Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental, vision, prescription)
* Flexible spending accounts & wellness programs
* Professional development & mentorship opportunities

To learn more about why UC is a great place to work, please visit our Careers Page.

**Job Summary:**

**The Department of Integrative Biology at Oregon State University (OSU) invites applications for three full-time (1.00 FTE), 9-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor positions in the field of integrative biology.**

Oregon State University is a public R1 research university and the largest university in the state of Oregon, with an enrollment of over 35,000 students and a sponsored project research budget of over 400 million dollars in 2025.

Within Oregon State, the College of Science is dedicated to research and education in exact and life sciences. The College is made of seven departments, deeply committed to upholding the values of inclusive excellence. Through our rich collection of people, ideas and perspectives, we engage in a healthy, constructive dialogue to learn, inform our research, and make discoveries.

Successful candidates are expected to develop vigorous, externally funded research programs with a primary focus on understanding processes within organisms that drive performance. Organismal-level research that is integrated with and/or has clear implications for ecological or evolutionary processes is preferred. Research may include theoretical, experimental, comparative and/or observational approaches in laboratory and/or field settings. The candidates will also contribute to a vibrant, inclusive and collaborative

department, including through mentorship of graduate and undergraduate students, teaching within the biology and zoology degree programs, and service to the university and profession.

More information about the department is available

at **http://ib.oregonstate.edu** .

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Scholarship and Creative Activity
* Teaching, Advising and Other Assigned Duties
* Service

**Qualifications:**
===================

**Required Qualifications:**

* Ph.D. (or foreign equivalent) in Biology or related field.

* Research with a primary focus on understanding processes within organisms that drive performance and may affect processes at ecological or evolutionary scales.
* Demonstrated ability or potential to establish an extramurally funded research program of high impact and longevity.
* Demonstrated ability or potential to instruct effectively using evidence-based practices at the undergraduate or graduate level
* Demonstrated ability or potential to mentor undergraduate and graduate students.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate with and engage with colleagues in a department, research or community group.

This position is designated as a critical or security-sensitive position; therefore, the incumbent must successfully complete a criminal history check and be determined to be position qualified as per University Standard: 05-010 et seq. jobs.title: Associate Professor Faculty Position in the School of Law, with a focus on Livable and Resilient Cities
jobs.description:
The School of Law at Boston University invites applications for a tenure-track Associate Professor position whose work is at the intersection of tax law and livable and resilient cities. This position is part of BU’s major investment in convergent research, bringing together bold ideas, deep expertise, and perspectives from across disciplines to take on society’s most critical challenges. We seek scholars examining how law and legal institutions shape the experience of cities and urban environments, with particular interest in tax law and its intersections with family, caregiving, inequality, and economic security. Areas of interest may also include discrimination, disability, healthcare decision-making, and personal autonomy. The successful candidate will contribute new perspectives on how legal structures can create or address disparities in economic, physical, and cognitive well-being across the life course.

The position is part of a University-wide cluster hire in Livable and Resilient Cities, which builds on BU’s strength in Urban Development & Resilience. Spanning anthropology, biology, civic data science, environmental health, journalism, learning sciences, political science, sociology, and urban affairs, the cluster draws together BU’s strengths in urban scholarship to advance new approaches to creating healthier, more equitable, and adaptable cities.

Boston University School of Law is a nationally recognized center for legal scholarship addressing complex challenges affecting health, well-being, and quality of life across the lifespan, with its Health Law program currently ranked No. 2 in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. Faculty conduct influential research on health law, bioethics, disability rights, aging, reproductive justice, public health, data privacy, and the regulation of emerging technologies, helping to shape law and policy at local, national, and global levels. Through interdisciplinary collaboration with scholars across medicine, public health, social work, and the sciences, BU Law advances evidence-based solutions that promote equitable access to care, protect vulnerable populations, and strengthen the legal and policy frameworks that support healthier lives and communities.

Since its founding in 1839, Boston University has embraced a mission of openness and access, becoming one of the first universities in the nation to welcome all students of ability regardless of race, gender, or creed. That tradition shapes our enduring commitment to academic freedom, free inquiry, and the robust exchange of ideas. Please visit https://www.bu.edu/values/ to learn more about our shared values.

We seek scholars who will contribute to our community of teachers and researchers through excellence in innovative scholarship, engaged teaching, and participation in the intellectual life of the University. Boston University provides an environment where faculty and students work together across disciplines, perspectives, and experiences to advance knowledge and address society’s most pressing challenges.

  
  
  
Required Skills  

**Position Qualifications**

Candidates should have a JD or equivalent degree in Law or a related field, a demonstrated ability to lead an independent research program, and a commitment to excellence and innovation in teaching, education, and mentorship of students. Successful candidates will be expected to actively engage in collaborative research; teach and mentor students; and provide rank-appropriate service to the department, university, and profession.

The salary allocated for these roles is $175,000 to $225,000. Final salary determination and rank placement will be based on the candidate's academic record, research background, years of qualifying experience, and a variety of other factors, including but not limited to licenses, specialty, departmental budgets, training and internal pay comparison. The stated hiring range represents the University's good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.

**Application Requirements**

Applicants should provide a personal statement that describes the candidate’s interest in both the convergent area of Livable and Resilient Cities and the department; a curriculum vitae; a research statement describing their research interests and experience; a teaching and mentoring statement detailing their approach to teaching and mentoring in an inclusive and diverse learning environment; and the names and contact information of 3 references at https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32922

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with a priority deadline of November 15. Applications will close November 30.

Only applications submitted via the above AJO link will be reviewed.

*Boston University is an equal opportunity employer.* *All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, age, national origin, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or* *identified* *in the University’s Notice of Non-Discrimination. Retaliation is also prohibited. We are a VEVRAA Federal Contractor. Under Massachusetts law, we may not* *require* *or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment.*

*Boston University, consistent with the AAU’s Principles on Preventing Sexual Harassment, conducts background checks for final candidates for certain faculty and staff positions. As part of this process, we ask current and past employers of the last seven years whether there has been a substantiated finding of sexual misconduct under their policies. To move forward, final candidates must complete and sign an “Authorization to Release Information” form after receiving an offer to enable this background check.*

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Architectural Design
jobs.description:
The Rice School of Architecture invites applications and nominations for a full-time, tenure-track faculty appointment at the rank of assistant professor with a focus in architectural design, to begin fall 2027.

  

The Rice School of Architecture welcomes and promotes the productive interrelationship of design practice and scholarship and is committed to supporting and advancing the voices of architects in academia. We seek outstanding design faculty who will pursue a focused design research agenda in areas that may include, but are not limited to, representation, materiality, or environment, at scales ranging from the building to the city. Successful candidates will teach undergraduate and graduate design studios, offer lecture courses and seminars in their areas of expertise, and conduct research and produce creative work of the highest caliber. Faculty are expected to bring a distinct voice, develop and sustain a clear line of inquiry, participate in the collective intellectual conversation of the faculty, and contribute to the advancement of the field of architecture more broadly.

  

As the fourth-largest and one of the most dynamic cities in the United States, Houston, Texas reflects the world’s most pressing challenges and is an exciting laboratory for new forms of architectural discourse and design agency. The Rice School of Architecture draws upon this unique context and Houston’s immense arts, culture, and industry, offering opportunities for both local and global engagement. Furthermore, the school’s position within a top-tier research university allows us to collaborate with other disciplines to forge new territories of critical practice and innovation.

  

Candidates should hold, at a minimum, a master of architecture degree or its equivalent (degree requirements must be fulfilled by July 1 of the year employment commences). Applications should include a letter of interest describing the candidate’s teaching, scholarship, and creative work and how they situate their work within larger disciplinary conversations; curriculum vitae; research/practice portfolio highlighting design, research, creative practice, and writing (20MB max.); teaching portfolio with sample syllabi and student work (20MB max.); and contact information for three professional/academic references who may be asked to provide a written letter of reference if candidacy is advanced to the next stage of the search process. The deadline for applications is December 30, 2026. To apply, please visit

jobs.title: Director, School of Computing
jobs.description:
**Director, School of Computing**
---------------------------------

**Search #:** 499857  
**Work type:** Full-time  
**Location:** UConn Storrs  
**Categories:** Faculty Tenure Track

**JOB SUMMARY**

**Director, School of Computing**

The University of Connecticut (UConn) invites applications for an exceptional academic leader and mentor to serve as the next Director of the School of Computing in the College of Engineering. This is a transformative opportunity to lead one of the University’s fastest-growing academic units and help shape the future of computing education and research at Connecticut’s flagship public research university. The anticipated start date is August 23, 2027.

The School of Computing is a vibrant community of scholars, educators, and students dedicated to advancing innovation across the computing disciplines. The School offers four rigorous bachelor’s degrees, two master’s degrees, a Ph.D. program, and a world-class research enterprise. Over the last 5 years, the School has experienced remarkable growth in enrollment, faculty recruitment, research funding, and scholarly impact, fostering new opportunities in areas such as cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and machine learning, bioinformatics, systems and networking, and data science analytics.

More than 1,300 undergraduate students and 150 graduate students benefit from a rigorous academic environment enriched by award-winning faculty, interdisciplinary collaboration, and numerous opportunities for experiential learning and research. The School is committed to educating the next generation of computing professionals and researchers while addressing pressing societal and technological challenges.

Founded in 1881, the University of Connecticut is a Carnegie R1 public research university and Connecticut's flagship institution of higher education. As a Land Grant and Sea Grant institution and a member of the Space Grant Consortium, UConn combines a proud tradition of public service with a global reputation for excellence in teaching, research, and innovation. The University serves more than 33,000 students across its main campus in Storrs, four regional campuses, the UConn School of Law in Hartford, and UConn Health in Farmington.

Consistently ranked among the nation's leading public universities, UConn is home to approximately 10,000 faculty and staff and is experiencing unprecedented momentum. Record application volumes, significant investments in research and infrastructure, and a steadfast commitment to student success have positioned the University for continued growth and impact. Through its mission of education, discovery, and engagement, UConn advances the social, economic, cultural, and environmental well-being of Connecticut and beyond.

The Director will provide strategic leadership for the School of Computing and will be responsible for advancing its educational, research, and service missions. The successful candidate will be a visionary and collaborative leader with a distinguished record of scholarly achievement, demonstrated administrative and management experience, and a commitment to fostering excellence across all aspects of the School. The Director will work closely with faculty, students, staff, alumni, industry partners, and university leadership to strengthen the School's national prominence, expand research opportunities, recruit and retain exceptional faculty and students, and cultivate an inclusive and supportive academic environment.

The successful candidate must possess credentials consistent with appointment as a tenured Full Professor in the College of Engineering and have a track record of leading a highly impactful, externally funded research program. They will demonstrate the ability to unite diverse perspectives, build consensus, and inspire innovation while stewarding the considerable strengths and resources of the School.

The successful candidate will receive a competitive compensation package, including appropriate research support and laboratory space.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Earned Ph.D. or equivalent in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or closely related discipline.
* An internationally recognized scholarly reputation and an outstanding record of external funding and research accomplishments. Applicants must, in particular, be qualified for an appointment at the rank of Professor.
* A clear and innovative academic vision for the School that encompasses its undergraduate, graduate, and professional educational enterprises.
* A clear vision of emerging research opportunities and an established track record of leadership in major efforts in research and/or education.
* Ability to foster productive relationships and collaborate effectively with faculty, students, staff, administrators, alumni, and external stakeholders.
* Strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience managing a budget and balancing multiple strategic priorities.
* Experience developing partnerships and collaborating with industry and government agencies.
* Demonstrated commitment to the success, growth and professional development of students, faculty, and staff.
* Dedication to fostering an environment that values diversity of perspectives.
* Experience recruiting, mentoring, and retaining talented faculty and support staff.
* Commitment to transparent, accessible, and collaborative leadership through open and effective communication.
* Demonstrated ability to serve as a strong advocate and ambassador for the School with institutional and external organizations.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**

The hiring range for this position is $240,000 to $260,000. An offer of employment, if made, will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s skill and experience, as determined by the University.

For more information about benefits and other offerings available to University employees, we encourage you to review the Human Resources website and explore the sections under the Benefits & Leaves and Engagement & Learning headers at the top of the page. Under Benefits & Leaves, select Benefits to access an overview as well as additional information on topics such as paid time off, benefits, retirement, and other resources. As you explore these pages, please note that this position is covered by the American Association of University Professors (AAUP) bargaining unit and look for information specifically identified as AAUP, as provisions may vary by employee group.

**APPOINTMENT TERMS**

This is a full-time, 10-month, tenured position at the rank of Full Professor with an anticipated start date of August 23, 2027. Applicants must meet University requirements for appointment at the rank of Full Professor, with tenure. The successful candidate’s primary academic appointment will be in the College of Engineering at the Storrs campus with the possibility of work at UConn's regional campuses across the state. Other rights, terms, and conditions of employment are contained in the collective bargaining agreement between the University of Connecticut and the American Association of University Professors UConn Chapter (AAUP).

**TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT**

Employment of the successful candidate is contingent upon the successful completion of a pre-employment criminal background check.

**TO APPLY**

Please apply online at Faculty and Staff Positions, **Search #499857** and submit the following application materials:

* **A cover letter**,
* Full **curriculum vitae**, including a complete record of funding and publications.
* A three-to-five-page career summary highlighting **research, scholarship, teaching, and service accomplishments**.

jobs.title: Open Rank/Open Tenure - Small Animal Educator, Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
jobs.description:
Clemson University: Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
  
  
Location
  
  
CVM - COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE HUB(001184) BLDG001184
  
  
Open Date
  
  
Sep 22, 2026
  
  
**Description**
The Clemson University Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine (PCVM) is seeking applicants for several full-time positions to serve as Small Animal Educators. These faculty positions will play a pivotal role in the development and implementation of the Clemson DVM curriculum (https://www.clemson.edu/veterinary-medicine/students/curriculum.html). The successful candidates will have a primary instructional role in developing and delivering small animal medicine and / or surgery content in the integrated Clemson DVM curriculum. These faculty members will teach with a dynamic, collaborative team consisting of experienced general practice clinicians, boarded specialists, and education specialists. The small animal medicine and surgery course series is designed to be an integrated, systems-based approach for conditions common to small animal general practice. This role is designed to attract outstanding educators and experienced clinicians who are passionate about teaching diagnostic medicine and small animal surgery in a practical, integrated fashion. Board certification in small animal internal medicine, small animal surgery, or ABVP certification is encouraged but not required.
  
  
The Clemson DVM curriculum is based upon integrative, collaborative team teaching in which faculty with varying backgrounds can work together to offer students an inclusive and innovative learning environment. The Small Animal Educators will collaborate with our other teaching faculty to facilitate vertical and horizontal integration for the delivery of core small animal internal medicine and surgery principles. Utilizing state of the art classrooms and teaching technology, this faculty member will be asked to adopt an integrated educational approach to provide students with a strong foundation of cognitive, clinical, and professional competencies in preparation for entry into the partially distributive model of clinical training in the fourth year. This position will consist primarily of didactic and small group instruction, along with some instruction in teaching laboratories. While the PCVM will not have a specialty referral hospital, it will have a fully staffed Community Practice as well as a robust Shelter Medicine spay-neuter program. The Small Animal Educators will work closely with the Community Practice and Shelter Medicine clinicians to integrate classroom concepts that translate seamlessly into real world experiences. A clinical service commitment is not required; however, interested individuals are encouraged to engage in teaching activities in our Community Practice. Additionally, these faculty members will engage in scholarly activity, which can include curriculum development, programmatic or curricular assessment, scholarship of teaching and learning, and other similar activities. Finally, a hybrid academic appointment will be considered for a boarded small animal specialist (internal medicine and / or surgery). If desired, this individual may seek a combination of a part-time academic appointment at Clemson while also having a part-time position in private referral practice. The possibility of a 9-month to 12-month contract are options that can be discussed with the Department Chair.
  
  
**Overview Of Clemson And The PCVM**
Located in South Carolina’s beautiful and fast-growing Upstate, Clemson University is the land-grant university of South Carolina and ranks among the country’s top 50 national public universities in the U.S. News & World Report. The University has nearly 23,400 students (including nearly 18,600 undergraduates) who can select from 80 undergraduate and 110 graduate degree programs. Clemson employs over 1,150 full-time faculty and has an annual budget expenditure of over $900M. Clemson University maintains its status as an R1 Carnegie Research Institution while maintaining a strong focus on undergraduate education.
  
  
The PCVM is currently seeking accreditation by the American Veterinary Medicine Association-Council on Education to offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree to approximately 80 students per cohort which started in August 2026). The PCVM plans to utilize a partial distributive model of clinical training for students. Its brand-new state of the art campus will reside in Pendleton, SC, near the T. Ed Garrison Arena, will house research and teaching labs, and utilize both ambulatory services as well as teaching sites at the Clemson University Equine Center, Lamaster Dairy Cattle Center, and other locations for education in the field.
  
  
In 2023, the Board of Trustees approved Clemson Elevate, the university’s new strategic plan. Clemson Elevate is built on 3 pillars: deliver the #1 student experience, double research by 2035, and transform lives statewide and beyond. The PCVM was named as a strategic priority for the university, demonstrating the importance of the new college to the future of the university and the state. We are excited to attract a team of top talent as we build the new college.
  
  
**Overview Of The Position**
Reporting to the Department Chair and working closely with the Foundational Sciences and Clinical Skills Leads, the small animal medicine educator will:
  
  

* Create and deliver the small animal content in the team-taught systems-based courses in the curriculum.
* Participate in teaching laboratories as agreed upon with colleagues and the department chair
* Develop assessment strategies in alignment with the overall competency-based curriculum.
* Collaborate with other faculty members to ensure integration of knowledge and skills across years and courses.
* Actively and effectively engage in student-centered instruction, coaching, and mentorship.
* Collaborate closely with the Clemson University Community Practice and with our partner clinics.
* Serve on PCVM and campus committees as an appointed or elected member.

**Additionally, The Faculty Member Must Have The Ability To**

* Emulate our PCVM cultural values including integrity, authenticity, respect, welcoming, trust, and collaboration.
* Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team, possess exemplary verbal and written communication skills, with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and function independently with limited supervision and guidance.
* Work in partnership with faculty and staff across multiple disciplines and functions across the college and university.
* Participate in research and scholarship initiatives designed to improve educational and professional outcomes.
* Demonstrate a commitment to the core values of Clemson University and specifically to community, engagement, belonging and accessibility (CEBA).

**Qualifications**

* DVM or equivalent with 3+ years of relevant experience.
* Applicants must demonstrate a strong foundation in small animal practice and the ability to teach clinical skills to veterinary students in classroom and laboratory/skills settings
* Board certification is not required; board-eligible/board-certified candidates are encouraged to apply.
* Commitment to excellence and creativity in education.
* Licensed or eligible for licensure to practice veterinary medicine in South Carolina and ability to obtain a DEA license.

**Preferred Qualifications Include**

* 5+ years of relevant experience in veterinary medicine or education.

jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Department of Health Policy and Management in the School of Public Health at Texas A&M University invites applications for up to two tenure-track or tenured faculty appointments in the field of health economics. The positions are open rank, with a preference for candidates who qualify for an appointment at the associate professor or professor level for one of the appointments.

These positions require candidates with strong research skills and excellent teaching ability. Successful candidates are expected to conduct independent and collaborative research, obtain extramural funding, maintain a robust publication record, and contribute to the Department’s educational programs. Additionally, these positions require the ability to work well with multi-disciplinary teams.

Faculty enjoy 9-month appointments that are fully funded (“hard money”), with effort typically allocated to research (50%), teaching (40%), and service (10%) responsibilities. The standard teaching load is four classes per academic year, with options for reduced teaching loads and/or additional (Summer) salary for faculty with extramural research funding.

We seek candidates conducting innovative research in any area of health economics, but preference will be given to candidates with research interests in healthcare financing and health insurance, aging and long-term care, population health, or pharmaceutical economics and technology value assessment.

Faculty rank will be determined by the qualifications and experience of the successful candidate(s). For candidates seeking a senior-level appointment, a track record of mentoring doctoral students and junior faculty and obtaining extramural funding is especially desirable.

About the Department of Health Policy & Management:

The department has 12 tenured and tenure-track faculty, 5 academic professional track faculty, and 3 professors of practice. It is home to more than 120 graduate students. Our Master of Health Administration (MHA) program is ranked as one of the top graduate health administration programs in the nation by U.S. News & World Report and has been continuously accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education (CAHME) since 2008. The MHA program offers both a residential and an executive track. The department additionally offers a PhD in Health Services Research and a Master of Public Health degree with a concentration in Health Policy & Management.

Furthermore, Department faculty teach in the School of Public Health’s Bachelor of Science in Public Health generalist degree program, which has more than 2000 majors.

The Department is committed to scholarly inquiry across a broad spectrum of areas. Faculty in the department represent a wide array of disciplines, expertise, and interests, with backgrounds in data science, economics, health services research, public health, political science, law, and management science. Faculty are highly collaborative, with substantial research strengths across a variety of areas, including health care access and delivery infrastructures, quality of health care services, chronic disease burden, maternal and child health, rural health, and data privacy. Ideally, a successful candidate’s research interests will align with one or more of the School of Public Health’s six research centers:

* Center for Community Health and Aging
* USA Center for Rural Public Health Preparedness
* Southwest Rural Health Research Center
* Ergonomics Center
* Center for Health & Nature
* Center for Health Equity & Evaluation Research

Additional Information:

Located in College Station, Texas, on the flagship campus of the Texas A&M University System, the CEPH-accredited School of Public Health has more than 95 faculty in four departments. Texas A&M University, a land-, sea-, and space-grant institution, was the state’s first public institution of higher learning, is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU) and boasts world-class resources available to all faculty.

The Department of Mining and Minerals Engineering at Virginia Tech invites applications for an open rank tenured or tenure-track faculty position in intelligent mining systems and automation. Areas of specific interest include, but are not limited to: mine systems, optimization and digitization; autonomous mining; robotics and intelligent machines; artificial intelligence and machine learning for mining applications; digital twins; human-machine interaction; analytics and real-time decision-making. We seek an innovative and collaborative scholar who will contribute to the department’s collegial, interdisciplinary environment and strengthen its longstanding excellence in fundamental and applied research, education, and engagement with the mining industry. Highly qualified and distinguished applicants may be eligible for a named professorship that will provide salary and operational support.

The recently renovated Holden Hall, the long-term home of the department, provides state-of-the-art facilities for department personnel, including the Autonomous Mining Arena. The department also enjoys close partnership with industry, and currently convenes the Built for the Mine partnership, an education and research-oriented collective that includes 12 leading mining technology companies and producers. The department currently has nearly 20 tenure-line, instructional, and research faculty members and is home to over 120 undergraduate and graduate students. The department’s teaching, research, and operations are centered around core values that include Technical Excellence, Leadership, Community, and Resilient Creativity.

The successful candidate will have a PhD in Mining Engineering or a closely related field at time of appointment, a strong record of academic accomplishments and a proven ability to work collaboratively, a commitment to interdisciplinary research and instruction, and a willingness to expand disciplinary boundaries to address complex technical and societal challenges. The successful candidate will have a high potential to build an independent, coherent, and robust area of scholarship; the ability to effectively advise PhD students, the ability to teach required undergraduate courses in our curriculum, and identify needs for and develop new courses.

Applicants must apply online at jobs.vt.edu. Candidates for this position must have a Ph.D. in Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Architectural Engineering,or a closely related field.
