jobs.title: Faculty, Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL)
jobs.description:
**Description**
**About Arkansas Colleges of Health Education**
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE) is a private, non-profit, graduate-level health sciences institution located on over 500 acres in Fort Smith, Arkansas. ACHE’s service-driven mission is to educate and train a diverse group of competent and compassionate healthcare professionals; to create health and research support facilities; and to provide healthy living environments to improve the lives of others. Founded in 2014, ACHE has experienced rapid growth and is poised to be a leader in healthcare education for years to come. ACHE is the first and only private institution in Arkansas that is dedicated solely to healthcare and wellness, and maintains a strong commitment to the surrounding community.
  
  
**About Fort Smith And The Arkansas River Valley**
Fort Smith is a vibrant community of around 90,000, with a low cost of living and ample recreational opportunities. Located in the beautiful Arkansas River Valley at the foothills of the Ozark mountains, Fort Smith is nestled between the Ozark-St. Francis and Ouachita National Forests. The region provides hiking, mountain biking, rock climbing, hang gliding, whitewater rafting, and camping all within a short drive. In addition, the city supports a variety of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, an award-winning symphony, and two historic entertainment districts.
  
  
**LOCATION**
This is a hybrid position. The employee will be remote the majority of the time, with the supervisor determining any residential requirements.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL) Faculty member is a collaborative educator and scholar committed to excellence in graduate education, executive leadership development, scholarship, service, and continuous program improvement.
  
  
The faculty member will contribute to the delivery and ongoing development of the Doctor of Executive Leadership program through high-quality online instruction, curriculum development, student advising and mentorship, scholarly activity, program assessment, and institutional and professional service.
  
  
The faculty member will work collaboratively with the DEL Program Director, faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership to support the mission, vision, goals, and continued growth of the DEL program and Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE).
  
  
The faculty member will carry a teaching load as assigned based on program needs and institutional expectations and will actively contribute to the academic, scholarly, and service missions of ACHE.
  
  
**Essential Functions And Responsibilities**
**Teaching and Curriculum**

* Teach online Doctor of Executive Leadership courses within areas of demonstrated academic or professional competence.
* Provide high-quality, engaging, doctoral-level instruction appropriate for experienced working professionals and executive leaders.
* Develop, review, and revise course content, instructional materials, learning activities, and assessments.
* Ensure alignment among course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, instructional activities, and assessments.
* Maintain current, evidence-informed course content reflecting contemporary leadership theory, organizational practice, healthcare, business, policy, and other relevant areas.
* Utilize effective online teaching methodologies and educational technologies to promote student engagement and learning.
* Provide timely, substantive, and constructive feedback on student assignments and academic performance.
* Maintain consistent course organization, communication, grading practices, and academic expectations.
* Participate in continuous curriculum review and improvement.
* Support the development of new DEL courses, concentrations, certificates, educational pathways, and other curricular initiatives as assigned.
* Maintain the security and integrity of course materials, assessments, student information, and academic records.
* Teach courses in other ACHE programs when appropriate based on expertise and institutional needs.

**Student Advising and Mentorship**

* Serve as an academic advisor and mentor to DEL students as assigned.
* Maintain appropriate availability and responsiveness to students.
* Monitor student academic progression and provide guidance when academic or professional development needs are identified.
* Provide individualized mentorship that connects doctoral education with students' professional leadership goals and organizational impact.
* Support students experiencing academic difficulty and participate in remediation activities when appropriate.
* Refer student concerns involving academic performance, professionalism, or conduct to the DEL Program Director in accordance with institutional policies.
* Support student scholarly activities, presentations, publications, professional development, and other academic opportunities.
* Promote a supportive, inclusive, professional, and academically rigorous learning environment.

**Scholarship and Research**

* Maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate to academic rank, professional expertise, and institutional expectations.
* Engage in research, applied scholarship, scholarly writing, peer-reviewed publication, professional presentations, or other recognized forms of scholarly activity.
* Pursue opportunities for collaborative scholarship with DEL faculty, ACHE faculty, students, and external partners.
* Mentor DEL students in scholarly inquiry, evidence-based leadership, research, and dissemination of scholarly work when appropriate.
* Participate in the development and evaluation of DEL program-related research and scholarly initiatives.
* Seek opportunities to translate research and professional experience into knowledge that advances executive leadership, organizational performance, healthcare, education, or other relevant fields.
* Pursue external funding, grants, or collaborative research opportunities when appropriate.
* Disseminate scholarly work at local, state, national, and international professional forums.

**Program Assessment and Continuous Improvement**

* Participate in the ongoing assessment and evaluation of the DEL curriculum and program.
* Assist with evaluation of course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, student performance, and other measures of program effectiveness.
* Participate in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of assessment data.
* Contribute to accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and continuous quality-improvement activities as assigned.
* Participate in periodic review and revision of course materials, curriculum, academic policies, and program processes.
* Provide recommendations to the DEL Program Director regarding opportunities to improve academic quality, student outcomes, and program effectiveness.
* Maintain required academic and administrative documentation in accordance with ACHE policies and applicable accreditation standards

**Program and Institutional Service**

* Serve as a member of DEL program committees and other ACHE committees as assigned.
* Participate in faculty meetings, curriculum meetings, assessment activities, retreats, and other institutional responsibilities.
* Participate in DEL admissions activities, including applicant review, interviews, and candidate evaluation as requested.
* Support DEL orientation, information sessions, recruitment events, student activities, and other program initiatives.
* Participate in faculty governance and institutional service activities consistent with academic appointment and institutional expectations.
* Collaborate with faculty and staff across ACHE programs to advance interdisciplinary education and institutional initiatives.
* Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of ACHE.
* Participate in commencement, academic ceremonies, institutional events, and other activities requiring faculty representation as appropriate.

**Recruitment and Program Growth**

* Support recruitment and enrollment initiatives for the DEL program.
* Participate in information sessions, webinars, conferences, professional meetings, and other recruitment activities as requested.
* Engage professional networks and organizations to increase awareness of the DEL program.
* Identify opportunities for educational partnerships, professional collaborations, and student recruitment.
* Support development of relationships with healthcare systems, academic institutions, professional organizations, government agencies, military organizations, nonprofit organizations, and other potential partners when appropriate.
* Assist in identifying emerging leadership-development needs and opportunities that may inform future DEL curriculum and program growth.

**Professional and External Engagement**

* Maintain active engagement within relevant professional and academic communities.
* Represent ACHE and the DEL program professionally at conferences, meetings, educational events, and community activities.
* Participate in local, state, regional, national, or international professional service appropriate to expertise and academic role.
* Develop relationships that may contribute to educational opportunities, research, scholarship, student development, or institutional partnerships.
* Maintain professional competence and remain current within areas of academic and professional expertise.

**Faculty Responsibilities And Professional Conduct**

* Maintain professional, ethical, and collegial relationships with students, faculty, staff, institutional leadership, and external partners.
* Demonstrate reliability, accountability, professionalism, and responsiveness in fulfilling assigned responsibilities.
* Adhere to ACHE policies and procedures and applicable academic, regulatory, accreditation, and ethical standards.
* Maintain confidentiality and privacy of student, faculty, and institutional information.
* Demonstrate respect for diverse perspectives, backgrounds, professional experiences, and areas of expertise.
* Contribute to a collaborative, solutions-focused, and professional faculty environment.
* Participate in faculty development and continuing professional education as appropriate.
* Complete required institutional training and administrative responsibilities in a timely manner.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the DEL Program Director, Dean, or their designee.

**Teaching Load**

* The DEL Faculty member will carry a teaching load as determined by the DEL Program Director and institutional leadership based on program needs, faculty workload expectations, areas of expertise, and other assigned responsibilities.
* Teaching assignments may include DEL courses as well as courses in other ACHE academic programs when appropriate, based on faculty expertise and institutional needs.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Program Director, Doctor of Executive Leadership or their designee.

**Requirements**
**QUALIFICATIONS AND CREDENTIALS**
**Education And Experience**
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Earned doctoral degree from an appropriately accredited institution in leadership, healthcare, business, education, organizational leadership, public administration, or another field relevant to the DEL curriculum.
* Credentials sufficient to qualify for academic appointment at the level of Assistant Professor or higher.
* Demonstrated experience in higher education, professional education, executive education, or a related academic environment.
* Demonstrated experience in leadership, administration, organizational management, healthcare, education, business, government, military leadership, or another area relevant to the DEL curriculum.
* Experience developing, managing, or teaching online or technology-enhanced curriculum.
* Evidence of commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarship, service, and student mentorship.
* Ability to contribute to doctoral-level education for experienced professionals and executive leaders.
* Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership.
* Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, organizational, and professional communication skills.
* Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of ACHE.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Significant progressive leadership or executive experience.
* Experience teaching at the doctoral or graduate level.
* Experience developing or delivering online doctoral education.
* Experience mentoring doctoral or graduate students.
* Record of peer-reviewed scholarship, professional presentations, applied research, or other scholarly activity.
* Experience with curriculum development, program assessment, accreditation, or institutional effectiveness.
* Experience working across disciplines or within complex organizations.
* Experience developing external partnerships, professional collaborations, or funded projects.
* Demonstrated national or international professional engagement within an area relevant to the DEL program.

Applications will continue to be accepted until this date. Position description
  
The Department of Statistics and the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) at the University of California, Berkeley, invite applications for a joint tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level. This position is expected to be 50% time in each of the Departments of EECS and Statistics, although an appointment at different percentages can be made by mutual agreement.
  
This position aims to build upon Berkeley's legacy at the intersection of statistics and computer science in the areas of Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). We seek exceptional candidates who will expand our strength in shared research areas of critical need, Trustworthy AI and Foundations of Statistical ML and AI, while supporting undergraduate and graduate teaching in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML).

The Berkeley Department of Statistics is part of the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It is consistently ranked as a top program in Statistics internationally. Since the inception of the Department in 1955, graduates and faculty of Berkeley have shaped the foundations and applications of Statistics, Data Science, and Machine Learning. The department is proud of our interdisciplinary and collaborative nature, with many faculty and students collaborating across fields such as biomedicine, public health, neuroscience, physical sciences, the social sciences, and computer science.

The EECS department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers one of the strongest research and instructional programs in this field anywhere in the world. Our key strength is our array of cross-disciplinary, team-driven projects. The integration of EE and CS forms the core, with strong interactions that extend into many other disciplines.

The School of Music at East Texas A&M invites applicants for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor in Music (Director of Bands and Instrumental Activities). The successful candidate will provide artistic, academic, and programmatic leadership for the University's band program while contributing to teaching, Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities (RSCA), recruitment, outreach, and service. The position includes a reduced teaching load to accommodate administrative duties, in consultation annually with the Director of the School of Music.

The School of Music at East Texas A&M serves approximately 240 music majors across instrumental, vocal, and keyboard areas and is fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). It offers baccalaureate and master's degrees in music education and performance, and a Bachelor of Arts in Music. The School of Music is housed in a $30 million music building completed in 2010 containing state-of-the-art recital and concert halls, studios, rehearsal halls, classrooms, and teaching areas.

The band program includes three concert bands, two jazz ensembles, and marching and athletic bands. The Wind Ensemble has performed at both regional and national College Band Directors National Association Conferences as well as the Texas Music Educators Association Clinic/Convention, most recently in 2018. The Wind Ensemble is also actively involved in commissioning and premiering new works from the nation’s leading composers. The Marching Band performs at all home games as well as exhibitions at marching contests such as the Texas State UIL Marching Band Contest and Bands of America Regionals and Grand Nationals Marching Festival.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Conduct the Wind Ensemble (top ensemble)
* Teach Graduate and Undergraduate Conducting
* Teach graduate coursework in instrumental repertoire and pedagogy
* Teach additional courses based upon the candidate’s area of expertise
* Organize and administer a comprehensive university band program including concert ensembles, marching band, jazz ensembles and athletic bands
* Provide overall leadership of the band staff and instrumental faculty, as well as program development
* Supervise budget management and fiscal responsibilities for division needs
* Recruit for the band and university at the regional and state level
* Promote the band and university at regional, state and national events
* Participate in creative and/or research activities consistent with all faculty appointments
* Participate in service activities consistent with all faculty appointments
* Other duties as assigned by the Director of the School of Music
* Participate in service activities consistent with all faculty appointments

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

* **Education:** Doctorate in Music Education, Conducting, or a closely related field from an accredited institution; equivalent university experience and demonstrated achievement maybe considered in lieu of the doctorate
* **Experience / Knowledge / Skills:** At least three (3) years of experience as either a Director or Assistant Director of Bands at the university level
* **Ability to:** Multi-task and work well as part of a team, manage budgets associated with an R2 institution, coordinate department-wide recruiting activities

**PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:**

* At least five (5) years of experience in university teaching

Hiring Department
  
  
Department of Veterinary Medicine & Surgery
  
  
**Job Description**
The
**College of Veterinary Medicine**
at MU is on a mission to educate and train outstanding clinicians and scientists, generate new knowledge, engage stakeholders, and foster economic growth, all of which promote and protect the health and welfare of animals and people. Our Doctor of Veterinary Medicine professional program boasts a unique curricular structure, which provides nearly two years of hands-on training in the college’s general and specialty clinics. Additionally, the College is a leader in the training of Undergraduate, Masters, and PhD students in the areas of Biomedical Sciences and Veterinary Pathobiology.
***Simply put, our mission is to Teach, Heal, Discover, and Serve.***
The
**Department of Veterinary Medicine and Surgery**
is dedicated to developing and disseminating knowledge to improve the health and well-being of animals and people through instruction, innovative research, service, and leadership. The department is home to the college’s
**Veterinary Health Center**
where our faculty provide clinical care, teach, and develop innovative treatments and therapies.
  
  
The
**Oncology Service**
in the MU College of Veterinary Medicine includes all three sub-specialties: medical, radiation, and surgical. The service is the second highest revenue generating service in our hospital, managing approximately 1,500 consultations every year. Comprised of four faculty members, the Medical Oncology team supervises six medical oncology residents annually, as well as contributes to the supervision and training of small animal rotating interns as well as oncology interns each year. In addition to patient care and treatment, house officer training, and DVM student education, the faculty in the service contribute to research activities both in the College of Veterinary Medicine, through public-private partnerships and clinical trials, and with the greater MU community through collaboration with the School of Medicine, the Ellis Fischel Cancer Center, and the NextGen Precision Medicine Initiative.
  
  
We are seeking an
**Assistant, Associate, or Full Tenure/Tenure Track Professor to join our Medical Oncology Service**
. Incumbents will be expected to maintain a strong caseload, participate in house officer training and DVM student education, as well as drive a robust translational research program that seeks to develop new and innovative treatments, improve diagnostic capabilities, increase patient outcomes, and drive understanding of cancer as a disease. They will be expected to participate in collaborative, interdisciplinary research efforts seeking to understand and treat cancer.
  
  
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Provide high-quality treatment and patient care as a member of the medical oncology service.
* Participate in the clinical and didactic teaching of veterinary students; modeling professional conduct and providing case-based instruction and feedback.
* Train, mentor, and guide house officers (both residents and interns), providing consistent instruction, feedback, coaching, and mentoring.
* Build and maintain a strong research program in an area of Veterinary Medical Oncology. The University of Missouri places a strong focus on interdisciplinary and collaborative research and values a One Health and Comparative Medine mindset and approach to research.
* Contribute to and participate in college, departmental and hospital governance and service through committee work and other activities.

This is a full-time, benefit eligible, 12-month/year appointment. Distribution of effort between teaching, research, and service will depend on the career goals of the final candidate and the needs of the department.
  
  
***This faculty opening is cross-posted with a Non-Tenure Track (Teaching / Clinical) Faculty Position in Veterinary Medical Oncology (Job ID 60797). There is one opening that may be filled at any level depending on final candidate qualifications.***
**Qualifications**
**Minimum Qualifications:**

* A Doctorate in Veterinary Medicine (DVM) or equivalent degree (such as VMD, BVSc)
* Successful completion of a residency training program approved by the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine, Specialty of Oncology or the European College of Veterinary Medicine, Specialty of Oncology prior to appointment start date

**Candidates Will Be Evaluated On**

* Diplomate status or eligibility for board certification by ACVIM, Specialty of Oncology or an equivalent authority
* Possession of an advanced degree (Masters or Doctoral level) is required
* Professional, residency and graduate training
* Prior research productivity and experience building and maintaining an externally funded, independent research program
* Educational and professional achievement, career goals and the needs of the college
* Eligibility for licensure to practice veterinary medicine in Missouri, DEA registration and BNDD certificate

Application Materials
  
  
**Interested Candidates Should Be Prepared To Attach**

* Letter stating professional interests and career goals
* Curriculum Vitae

Please contact Noah Hartsfield, HR Recruiter, at hartsfieldn@missouri.edu or 573-882-3761 or Dr. Lee Talbott, Search Committee Chair at jtalbott@missouri.edu.
  
  
Sponsorship Information
  
  
Employment visa sponsorship may be available for candidates currently in the United States in H-1B status or other work-authorized status.
  
  
Community Information
  
  
**MU is a nationally competitive, global university.**
Many states fund separate research and land-grant universities, but Missouri combines those roles at its flagship institution. MU is both a land-grant university with a statewide mission of service to citizens and Missouri’s largest public research university. Mizzou is one of only five universities nationwide that offers law, medicine, veterinary medicine, and a nuclear research reactor on one campus.
  
  
**About**
**MU is a national leader in comparative medicine,**
in which researchers collaborate by sharing discoveries, innovations and treatments for humans and animals. For more about the College of Veterinary Medicine and our impact on Missouri, the nation, and the world, go to:
  
  

* University of Missouri/College of Veterinary Medicine - http://cvm.missouri.edu/
* Veterinary Health Center - http://www.vmth.missouri.edu/
* Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Lab - http://vmdl.missouri.edu/

**Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and a high quality of life for people of all ages and interests.**
Founded on education and known as an ideal college town, its location also makes it an attractive spot for businesses and travelers. Located on Interstate 70 and U.S. Highway 63, Columbia is right in the middle of the state and the nation. Just a couple hours’ drive from St. Louis and Kansas City, Columbia is Boone County’s largest population center offering big-city culture, activities, and resources with a low cost of living. Columbia is home to a variety of restaurants and entertainment venues and hosts more than a dozen festivals each year. If you want to grow your career, continue your education, raise a family, and retire, Columbia is a good place to be!
  
  
Benefit Eligibility
  
  
This position is eligible for University benefits. As part of your total compensation, the University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, and educational fee discounts for all four UM System campuses. For additional information on University benefits, please visit the Faculty & Staff Benefits website at https://www.umsystem.edu/departments-staff/human-resources/benefits-retirement

**SUMMARY:**

The School of Music at East Texas A&M University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track **Assistant/Associate Professor in Music (Director of Choral Activities)**. The successful candidate will provide artistic, academic, and programmatic leadership for the University's choral program while contributing to teaching, Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities (RSCA), recruitment, outreach, and service. The position includes a reduced teaching load to accommodate administrative duties, in consultation annually with the Director of the School of Music.

The School of Music serves approximately 240 music majors across instrumental, vocal, and keyboard areas and is fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). It offers baccalaureate and master's degrees in music education and performance and a Bachelor of Arts in Music. The School is housed in a $30 million music building completed in 2010 containing state-of-the-art recital and concert halls, studios, rehearsal halls, classrooms, and teaching areas.

The University Chorale has an established record of significant artistic and educational achievement, including performances at Carnegie Hall, the International Music Festival of Campina Grande in Brazil, venues in France and Austria, and the 2019 Texas Music Educators Association Convention.

The Director will lead the University Chorale and Chamber Singers; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in choral conducting, choral literature, and related areas; mentor students; and contribute to the continued growth, visibility, and reputation of the choral program through high-quality performance, programming, recruitment, outreach, and professional engagement.

The position includes an administrative release; duties will be determined based on qualifications, administrative experience, demonstrated leadership skills, and School of Music needs.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Choral Program Leadership and Artistic Direction**

* Provide artistic, educational, and programmatic leadership for the University's choral program.
* Direct the University Chorale and Chamber Singers and oversee their artistic development, rehearsal, performance, and long-term growth.
* Establish high standards for ensemble musicianship, vocal technique, diction, interpretation, and performance.
* Develop an artistic vision and select repertoire representing a breadth of historical periods, styles, composers, languages, and world/cultural contexts.
* Plan concert programming and pursue appropriate performance, touring, festival, conference, and collaborative opportunities.
* Participate in strategic planning and program development for the continued growth of choral activities.

**Teaching and Student Development**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in choral conducting, choral literature, and related areas as assigned.
* Provide instruction in conducting technique, score study, rehearsal methodology, choral pedagogy, repertoire, and ensemble leadership.
* Mentor and advise students pursuing careers in music education, conducting, performance, and related fields.
* Contribute to curriculum development, assessment, and program review within the choral area and School of Music.

**Music Education and Professional Preparation**

* Work with music education faculty to prepare students for careers as music educators and choral professionals.
* Supervise and mentor student teachers and maintain relationships with cooperating teachers and school administrators.
* Provide students with opportunities to develop professional skills in choral teaching and conducting.

**Recruitment, Retention, and Outreach**

* Provide leadership for recruitment and retention of undergraduate and graduate students in choral music, music education, performance, conducting, and related areas.

**PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:**

jobs.description:
LaGrange College seeks to fill a tenure-track position at the assistant professor level in Religious Studies beginning August 1, 2027. The field of specialization is open, but preference will be given to candidates who can teach Christian ethics and broader philosophical approaches to ethics including Bioethics and possibly business ethics and the ethics of AI, as well as candidates prepared to contribute in areas such as American Christianity or world religious traditions.
  
  
A Ph.D. in religious studies or related field is required, although outstanding ABD candidates will be considered. The successful candidate must have their terminal degree completed prior to the end of their second year in the position.
  
  
The teaching load is four (4) courses per semester, including introductory courses, upper-level electives in the candidate’s field(s) of specialization, and courses that satisfy the college’s general education curriculum, known as Ethos. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to help shape the future of the major in religion and help create interdisciplinary approaches to critical analyses of American culture and society. The position includes the supervision and mentorship of undergraduate research projects in the field. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching, professional development, and institutional service, as well as an understanding of, and appreciation for, the mission of liberal arts institutions.
  
  
The religion program maintains a close relationship with the Candler School of Theology at Emory University; students interested in a future ministry career will find a direct and accelerated pathway from LaGrange College to the Candler School of Theology. Through both a solid grounding in theory and engagement in the field (via internships, collaborative undergraduate research, and other opportunities) Religious Studies students receive a thorough, intensive, and experiential education in the discipline. The program’s historic engagement in LaGrange College’s undergraduate research program affords students the opportunity to work directly with faculty on research projects that build their professional skills. The college values its relationship with the United Methodist Church and in particular its commitment to the Wesleyan ideal of service.
  
  
Interested candidates should visit https://lagrangecollege.applicantstack.com/x/openings to apply for the position and to view other positions available at the college. Required documents include:
  
  

* A letter of interest describing the alignment of the candidate’s qualifications with the position requirements

Review of applications will begin Nov. 9 and will continue until the position is filled.

jobs.description:
* Pensacola - Main Campus, Florida, United States

* Dept of Art and Design

* College of Arts, Social Sciences & Humanities

#### **POSITION DETAILS**

**Employment based visa sponsorship will be considered for this position.**

**Position Number:** 105770
  
**Classification Title:** Assistant Professor
  
**Working Title:** Assistant Professor of Museum Studies
  
  
**Department:** Dept of Art and Design
  
**FLSA Status:** Exempt
  
**Salary Range:** Commensurate with education and experience
  
**Pay Basis:** Annually

#### **POSITION OVERVIEW**

##### **JOB SUMMARY:**

The University of West Florida Department of Art & Design invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Museum Studies. This position will play a central role in developing the new interdisciplinary Minor in Museum Studies and expanding the Art History Major into Museum Studies, both designed to provide students with foundational knowledge and hands-on experience in museums, galleries, collections management, exhibition production, interpretation, preparatorship, and public-facing cultural work. The salary for this position will be commensurate with education and experience.
  
  
This initiative supports the university’s area of expertise in Public Archaeology and Community Heritage and is intended to serve undergraduate and graduate students in Art, Art History, History, Archaeology, Anthropology, Public History, Graphic Design, Arts Administration, and related disciplines. The program will leverage the University’s unique partnerships and resources, including TAG, The Art Gallery at UWF, the Pensacola Museum of Art, the Pensacola Museum of History, the Pensacola Children’s Museum, the UWF Historic Trust, the UWF Archaeology Institute, and the Florida Public Archaeology Network (FPAN).
  
  
The successful candidate will contribute to the development and growth of the Museum Studies Minor and Art History and Museum Studies Major while also helping to guide The Art Gallery at UWF (TAG) as a teaching gallery, exhibition space, and experiential learning site. The position emphasizes interdisciplinary learning, applied museum practice, and student-centered professional development through coursework, internships, exhibitions, collections work, public programming, and collaborative cultural projects.
  
  
The faculty member will be housed in the Department of Art & Design in the College of Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities at the University of West Florida. The Department is strongly committed to fostering a welcoming, collaborative, and student-centered learning environment grounded in interdisciplinary practice, experiential learning, and community engagement.
  
  
Position Responsibilities:
  
  
This is a full-time, tenure-earning position with benefits. The successful candidate will contribute to developing an interdisciplinary Museum Studies Minor and an Art History and Museum Studies Major, teaching courses across museum studies, curatorial practice, gallery operations, collections management, museum education, public history, and audience engagement.
  
  
Teaching responsibilities may include undergraduate courses within the Department of Art & Design, as well as courses that support interdisciplinary connections with History, Public History, Archaeology, Anthropology, Art Administration and related majors and programs. Depending on the candidate’s expertise, courses may address topics such as:
  
  

* Museum Studies
* Exhibition Practices
* Curatorial Methods
* Collections Management
* Museum Education and Interpretation
* Gallery Operations
* Preparatorship and Exhibition Installation
* Public History and Community Heritage
* Museum Writing and Audience Engagement
* Digital Interpretation and Public-Facing Cultural Work
* Art History
* Architectural History

  
The successful candidate should demonstrate the ability to curate exhibitions and develop exhibition-related learning opportunities in collaboration with TAG, the Pensacola Museum of Art, the UWF Historic Trust, the UWF Archaeology Institute, FPAN, and other regional museums, galleries, archives, archaeological organizations, and cultural institutions.
  
  
Experiential Learning & Museum and Gallery Engagement:
  
  
The position connects classroom learning directly to applied gallery and museum practice by guiding exhibitions as teaching opportunities and experiential learning sites, coordinating exhibition and experiential learning opportunities through partnerships with TAG, The Art Gallery at UWF, the Pensacola Museum of Art, the Pensacola Museum of History, the Pensacola Children’s Museum, the UWF Historic Trust, the UWF Archaeology Institute, and the Florida Public Archaeology Network (FPAN). The faculty member will coordinate the department's experiential learning ecosystem and provide mentorship across all stages of exhibition production. This includes leading student-centered initiatives such as exhibition and event graphic design, administrative and preparatorial operations, and an annual faculty-partnered exhibition series that connects coursework with faculty research. Together, these opportunities allow students to engage in the full lifecycle of exhibitions—from concept development and design to installation, programming, and documentation—as the Assistant Professor strengthens curricular connections and expands partnerships with regional cultural institutions.

##### **MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

Holds the highest degree appropriate in Museum Studies, Art History, Public History, Anthropology, Archaeology, Arts Administration, Exhibition Design, Curatorial Studies, or a related field, or possesses equivalent qualifications based on professional experience, and be otherwise qualified to perform assigned duties. The appointee engages in teaching, scholarship and creative projects, and/or service and other related activities.

##### **POSITION QUALIFICATIONS:**

Terminal degree, PhD, MFA, or equivalent, in Museum Studies, Art History, Public History, Anthropology, Archaeology, Arts Administration, Exhibition Design, Curatorial Studies, or a related field, completed by the start date of appointment.
  
  
Professional experience in museums, galleries, archives, collections, cultural institutions, exhibition spaces, or related organizations.
  
Teaching experience at the university level or demonstrated potential for effective undergraduate teaching.
  
  
Demonstrated ability to support gallery, museum, exhibition, collections-based, or public-facing cultural learning experiences for undergraduate students.
  
  
Demonstrated commitment to experiential learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and student professional development.

##### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

Experience developing or teaching interdisciplinary Museum Studies coursework.
  
  
Experience directing, managing, or coordinating a museum, university gallery, exhibition space, archive, collection, cultural program, or public-facing arts initiative.
  
  
Experience with exhibition production, collections management, curatorial practice, museum education, preparatorship, archives, public programming, or cultural heritage interpretation.
  
  
Experience curating exhibitions or developing exhibition-related projects in collaboration with museums, galleries, archives, archaeological organizations, public history sites, community-based cultural institutions, or university partners.
  
  
Experience supporting experiential learning, internships, undergraduate research, project-based learning, or high-impact educational practices.
  
Experience mentoring students in applied museum, gallery, exhibition, design, archival, or public history contexts.
  
  
Ability to contribute to interdisciplinary collaboration across Art, Art History, Graphic Design, History, Archaeology, Anthropology, Public History, Arts Administration, and related fields.
  
  
Experience working with student exhibition teams, design teams, preparator teams, gallery interns, or museum education programs.
  
  
Experience teaching in multiple modalities, including in-person and online instruction.

##### **PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* **Physical Requirements:** Regularly involves lifting, bending or other physical exertion. Often exposed to one or more disagreeable environmental factors, such as heat, cold, noise, dust, dirt, chemicals, etc., with often to the point of being objectionable.
* **Impact of Deadlines:** Routine deadlines. Usually sufficient lead time. Variance in work volume, seasonal, and predictable. Priorities can be anticipated. Some interruptions are present. Involves occasional exposure to demands/pressures from persons other than immediate sup.

**Special Requirements or Considerations of the Job:**

**Special Instructions to Applicants:** Candidates must apply online through the University of West Florida website: https://careers.uwf.edu. Applicants are required to attach a cv, letter of interest and contact information for three references. References will be contacted upon submission of this application. An opportunity to upload these documents will be provided during the application process. For assistance, please contact Human Resources at 850.474.2694 or email jobs@uwf.edu.
  
  
If one or more of your advanced degrees is awarded from an institution outside of the United States, UWF will require a credential evaluation and/or translation prior to onboarding. This credential evaluation should include original documents received directly from your institution so that the agency can evaluate and attest that your credential is equivalent to a similar degree earned at a US institution. jobs.description:
PCN 2094

**Position Overview:**

The Girard School of Business at Merrimack College invites applications for a full-time, open-rank, Non-Tenure Track (NTT) faculty position in Marketing beginning in Fall 2027.

The Girard School is seeking a faculty member who can help build a distinctive model of business education and applied scholarship at the intersection of marketing, analytics, artificial intelligence, technology, and the future of work. We are particularly interested in candidates who combine meaningful professional or industry experience with a strong commitment to teaching, scholarship, and external engagement.

This position is part of a broader strategic investment in faculty, research, experiential learning, and industry engagement within the Girard School. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to play a formative role in the development of the School's emerging Center for the Future of Work, an interdisciplinary research and engagement platform focused on understanding how technological, economic, demographic, and other forces are reshaping work and organizations.

Located in the Merrimack Valley, the School is particularly interested in leveraging the region's concentration of companies, industries, communities, and organizations as a setting for applied inquiry and partnership, while building relationships that extend nationally and globally.

The Center will seek to bridge academic inquiry and industry practice by working directly with organizations to identify consequential challenges, conduct applied research, engage students in real-world problem solving, and translate insights into scholarship, teaching, and broader thought leadership. The Center's work will be complemented by Applied Industry Labs that bring faculty, students, and industry partners together around real-world organizational and industry challenges.

**Responsibilities**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate Marketing courses consistent with the candidate's expertise and the needs of the Girard School, including courses related to marketing analytics and/or emerging technologies;
* Maintain an active program of applied scholarship and thought leadership focused on consequential problems facing organizations and industries. Relevant outputs may include applied research, white papers, industry reports, case studies, conference presentations, practitioner publications, and other work that advances knowledge and informs practice; ;
* Develop relationships with companies and other external organizations that can support research, experiential learning, and student engagement;
* Translate industry challenges and organizational data into opportunities for faculty research, student projects, cases, simulations, and other forms of applied learning;
* Contribute to the development of the Center for the Future of Work, related Applied Industry Labs, and the Girard School's broader capabilities in analytics and data-informed decision-making;
* Mentor undergraduate and graduate students and engage students meaningfully in research and applied projects;
* Contribute to the intellectual life, service, and strategic development of the Girard School and Merrimack College.

**Qualifications**

We are especially interested in candidates who are comfortable operating across academic and industry environments—individuals who can engage executives and organizational leaders, identify important questions emerging from practice, study those questions rigorously, and bring the resulting insights into the classroom and scholarly community.

The Girard School welcomes candidates whose careers have crossed traditional boundaries between industry and academia, including accomplished executives and senior practitioners who have developed or are developing a substantive scholarly and teaching agenda.

Relevant areas of scholarly and professional interest may include, but are not limited to:

* marketing analytics and data-driven decision-making;
* artificial intelligence and marketing;
* consumer analytics and customer insights;
* digital marketing and emerging technologies;
* marketing technology and automation;
* customer experience and personalization;
* AI-enabled communication and content creation;
* human-AI collaboration in marketing decision-making;
* responsible use of AI, data, and algorithms in markets; and
* the changing role and skills of marketing professionals.

Candidates need not specialize in all—or any particular combination—of these areas. Of greater importance is an intellectual agenda that addresses consequential problems facing contemporary organizations and lends itself to meaningful engagement with industry.

**Required Qualifications**

* A doctorate or appropriate terminal degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Analytics, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
* Demonstrated ability or strong potential to teach effectively at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
* Evidence of an active or emerging scholarly agenda, appropriate to the candidate's career stage, with interest in producing applied scholarship that addresses consequential organizational, market, or industry challenges.
* Demonstrated interest in engaging organizations and translating real-world challenges into scholarship and/or student learning.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Significant professional or industry experience in marketing, analytics, consumer insights, technology, consulting, digital strategy, or related areas.
* Experience applying analytics, artificial intelligence, or marketing technologies to organizational problems and decision-making.
* A record of applied research, thought leadership, industry presentations, or other work that bridges scholarship and practice.
* Experience developing relationships across industry, academia, or regional economic ecosystems.
* Interest in building new programs, research initiatives, partnerships, or experiential-learning models.
* Evidence of the ability to engage students from varied academic and professional backgrounds.

**Application Materials Should Include:**

* Curriculum vitae
* Cover letter stating motivation and interest in the position, citing experience relevant to the qualifications and experience associated with key responsibilities for the position including teaching philosophy and evaluations.
* Contact information for three professional references (name, title, address, phone number, email address). References will be contacted only at a later stage of the search process.

**Compensation**

The expected 9-month base salary range for the Assistant Professor or Assistant Professor of Practice rank is $80,000-$110,000; for the Associate Professor or Associate Professor of Practice $110,000,000-$130,000; for the Professor or Professor of Practice $130,000-$150,000. The actual pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate qualifications and prior experience, scope of responsibilities, internal equity, and market considerations.

**Work Location**

This is an on-campus position as employees are essential in order to provide a fully on-campus,

residential college experience for our students and the community.

This position is subject to the successful completion of a criminal background check.

**Statement on Our Mission**

Merrimack College is a Catholic Augustinian institution of higher education committed to building an accepting and respectful community. Our mission is to enlighten minds, engage hearts and empower lives and is inspired by our Catholic faith and the Augustinian tradition of seeking truth through inquiry and dialogue.

Merrimack College seeks candidates who understand, respect, and can contribute to Merrimack’s Catholic and Augustinian mission. All candidates should describe in their application how they will foster a culture that supports our mission.

**About Merrimack College**

The only Catholic, Augustinian institution of higher education in New England, Merrimack College is a private, independent, coeducational institution with more than 4,100 undergraduate, 2,500 graduate students and 50 doctoral students from 48 states and 63 countries. The College features more than 160 career-focused undergraduate, professional and graduate programs, all taught by exceptional faculty who are passionate about their subject and student success. The College has six schools: arts and sciences, engineering and computational sciences, nursing and health sciences, education and social policy, the Girard school of business and the graduate school of counseling and social work. The College’s suburban 220-acre campus is just north of Boston in North Andover, Massachusetts. Merrimack is a Master’s Colleges and Universities/Larger Programs (M1) institution in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. Merrimack is one of the fastest growing educational institutions in the country and has steadily climbed up in the U.S. News & World Report’s ranking of Best Colleges, ranking 38th in the Regional Universities North category in 2026. Merrimack is a NCAA Division I athletic institution.

Merrimack College is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track: Assistant Professor of Theatrical Production Management and Research
jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a full-time, 9-month tenure-track position in Theatrical Production Management and Research at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Dance, Music, and Theatre Performance section. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for scholarly achievement and an ability to establish a nationally and internationally recognized agenda for research and creative work focused on producing and researching structures that make interdisciplinary, virtual/hybrid, media-integrated, and devised performance possible. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to:

* Digital Transformation and Technology

* producing and scheduling systems for media-integrated and technology-driven performance

* live streaming, virtual and hybrid producing models

* data analytics for production planning, budgeting, and audience/venue operations

* Collaborative and Non-hierarchical Producing Models

* producing structures for devised and collectively created work, where authorship and decision-making are distributed rather than script-first

* Sound and Media Design as Producing Practice

* sound design, projection/media design, and live media integration as both creative and infrastructural components of production

* Interdisciplinary Partnerships

* producing collaborations across the theatre, dance, music, and visualization programs

* engaging with emerging technology across PVFA

This position supports the College's Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre, a practice-based, devised-theatre program established in Fall 2024, and complements the program's existing technical design faculty. Successful candidates will teach Stage Management and Producing Theatre and other courses as assigned that fall within their expertise. Preference will be given to candidates who also have experience in sound and/or new media design and an interest in advancing those design dimensions of the program.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

* Establish an active, nationally and internationally visible program of research and/or creative practice investigating production management as a discipline of its own — including its digital, collaborative, and technological dimensions

* Pursue external funding to support this agenda (e.g., NEA, NEH, foundation, or industry-partnered support for producing technology, digital infrastructure, or interdisciplinary production research)

* Disseminate work through exhibitions, performances, publications, presentations, software systems, patents, or other recognized scholarly outcomes

* Contribute production-management expertise to PVFA's theatre curriculum and season, and possibly sound and/or new media design expertise, as a site for applied research and graduate/undergraduate mentorship

* Build interdisciplinary partnerships that extend production-management research into visualization, data science, or technology domains represented elsewhere in the College

* Contribute to section, college, and university service

About the College

The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts was formed in 2022 at Texas A&M University, bringing together the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. PVFA is built without departments. Faculty sections and academic programs sit at the college level, which places musicians, composers, actors, directors, choreographers, dancers, painters, cinematographers, technical artists, level designers, spatial audio engineers, tools programmers, ethnomusicologists, art historians, UI/UX designers, and virtual set designers in one structure rather than in separate units. The College places a heavy emphasis on collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research.

The College offers the BS, MS, and MFA in Visualization, a PhD in Visual Computing and Interactive Media, and degree programs in music, dance, and theatre. It operates at the main campus in Bryan-College Station and as part of Texas A&M – Fort Worth, with facilities equipped for work at the intersection of the arts and emerging technology. Applicants should consult the college's website (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/) to review our academic and research programs.

##### **Description**

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a tenure-track, full-time, 9-month Assistant Professor of Art & Design in Intelligent Systems and Computational Design position in the Art & Design (ARTD) Section of the Visualization Program. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

The ARTD Section seeks an artist and/or designer whose work advances contemporary creative practice by blending intelligent systems, computational design, and generative methodologies as primary modes of artistic and design inquiry. We are particularly interested in candidates whose creative and scholarly work explores generative systems, machine learning, creative coding, computational creativity, and emerging forms of AI-enabled artistic and design production.

We seek candidates whose work investigates the creative, cultural, aesthetic, and critical possibilities of machine learning, generative AI, algorithmic systems, computational visualization, procedural design, and related computational approaches to art and design.

The Section welcomes research and creative practice across areas including:

* Artificial Intelligence and Creative Practice
    
  Creative applications of intelligent systems and machine learning, human-AI collaboration, computational creativity, and emerging approaches to artistic and design production.

* Computational Design
    
  Algorithmic design, creative coding, procedural systems, computational visualization, generative workflows, and computational methods for design innovation.

* Critical and Experimental Futures
    
  Research and creative work, including publications, that examines the cultural, social, ethical, and aesthetic implications of AI and computational technologies.

Across these areas, we are interested in how computation functions not simply as a tool, but as a medium for artistic inquiry, design research, experimentation, and creative production. We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate how intelligent systems, generative methodologies, and computational design function as conceptual, aesthetic, and material frameworks for contemporary artistic and design practice.

Computational and AI-driven practices may result in a wide range of outcomes, including screen-based experiences, physical artifacts, fabricated objects, spatial installations, immersive environments, performances, and hybrid digital-physical works. Consistent with the interdisciplinary mission of the College, we value candidates who demonstrate the ability to collaborate across art, design, visualization, computing, engineering, architecture, the humanities, performance, and the performing arts to produce meaningful creative, scholarly, and public-facing work.

The successful candidate will develop and maintain an active, externally recognized program of creative practice and/or research; contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in intelligent systems, computational design, generative creative practice, and contemporary art and design methodologies; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; develop innovative curriculum; and contribute to academic service.

The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with their areas of expertise, which may include artificial intelligence for creative practice, generative design, computational design, creative coding, computational visualization, digital fabrication, digital sculpture, and studio-based creative practice; advise and mentor MFA students; contribute to the continued evolution of graduate studio-based research and creative practice within the Visualization Program; participate in collaborative and interdisciplinary activities; and serve the profession, the program, and the university community.
