jobs.description:
**Overview**
The Alvin I. Goodman Chair in Nephrology ("Goodman Chair") is an endowed position in the Department of Medicine at New York Medical College (NYMC) School of Medicine (SOM) for a physician scientist with specialization in nephrology, kidney transplantation, kidney biology, renal injury and repair, translational immunology, and/or closely related disciplines. Candidates for the position shall hold and/or be eligible for an NYMC SOM faculty appointment at the rank of professor, and shall be eligible for clinical appointment to the medical staff at Westchester Medical Center (WMC), the primary academic clinical affiliate of NYMC. The Goodman Chair is expected to build a nationally recognized, externally funded translational research program that advances kidney science, discovery, and academic nephrology as relates to their area(s) of specialization. The endowment opportunity provides funds, with appropriate approvals, to support the compensation of the holder of the Goodman Chair, as well as research and teaching activities conducted under the holder’s.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Develops, leads, and sustains a nationally recognized translational research program in nephrology, or closely related disciplines/ areas of study, such as transplantation biology, renal injury and repair, epithelial and/or endothelial biology, translational immunology, etc.
* Secures, maintains, and expands extramural research support from federal agencies, foundations, industry partners, philanthropy, and other mission-aligned sources to support investigator-initiated science, collaborative programs, research infrastructure, trainee development, and endowed chair activities.
* Leads development of competitive grant applications, program-project proposals, center-level initiatives, industry-sponsored and investigator-initiated studies, philanthropic proposals, and endowment opportunities that advance NYMC and WMC priorities in kidney disease, transplantation, and translational biology.
* Demonstrates sustained scholarly and research productivity through peer-reviewed publications, national and international presentations, collaborative grants, trainee mentorship, and scientific leadership.
* Is expected to achieve a defined level of research productivity and financial sustainability within the first five years of appointment, including a substantial portfolio of investigator-initiated extramural funding sufficient to support the Chair holder’s research program, key research personnel, and ongoing scholarly activity.
* Builds collaborative research programs across the academic health center including the WMCHealth network, basic science and clinical departments, and external partners with priority to advance kidney disease, transplantation, dialysis, and vascular/endothelial biology research.
* Provides academic leadership for research and teaching activities supported by endowment funds, ensuring that resources are used for NYMC-approved research, educational, and scholarly activities conducted under the Chair holder’s direction.
* Mentors faculty, fellows, residents, medical students, graduate students, postdoctoral trainees, and research staff, with emphasis on career development, grant preparation, responsible conduct of research, and team-based translational science.
* Participates in NYMC and WMC clinical faculty activities appropriate to expertise, including consultation, program development, academic conferences, and collaboration with nephrology, transplantation, critical care, and related clinical programs.
* Engages in teaching within the SOM, Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, fellowship programs, and other NYMC educational programs as requested by the Department Chair and consistent with the Chair holder’s expertise.
* Adheres to all applicable federal, state, institutional, and sponsor requirements governing human subjects research, animal research, biosafety, data integrity, research compliance, reporting, and data sharing.
* Represents NYMC and WMC in regional, national, and international forums related to academic nephrology and/or closely related disciplines.
* Maintains continued eligibility for the Goodman Chair through sustained academic productivity, responsible stewardship of endowed resources, compliance with applicable policies and gift terms, active alignment with the endowed chair purpose, and satisfactory periodic review by the Department Chair and Dean of the SOM.

**Endowed Chair Stewardship Expectations**

* Develops, within the first year of appointment, a written five-year research, funding, recruitment, and program-development plan aligned with NYMC priorities, WMC clinical and translational missions, and the donor intent of the endowment.
* Uses endowed resources responsibly and transparently for allowable NYMC-approved purposes, including salary support where permitted, research personnel, trainees, pilot studies, core services, equipment, grant development, scholarly travel, academic programming, and research or teaching activities conducted under the Chair holder’s direction.
* Partners with NYMC, WMC, WMCHealth, and institutional advancement or philanthropy leadership to cultivate federal, foundation, industry, philanthropic, and continued endowment support for academic nephrology, kidney science and related work.
* Participates in donor stewardship, philanthropic engagement, public-facing academic presentations, investiture or recognition activities, and annual reporting that demonstrates the academic, scientific, educational, and clinical impact of the endowed chair.
* Provides an annual endowed chair impact report summarizing grants submitted and awarded, publications, invited presentations, trainees and junior faculty mentored, research staff supported, collaborations developed, philanthropy-related activities, use of endowed funds, and progress toward five-year goals.
* Builds a sustainable, cross-cutting translational research enterprise that extends beyond a single disease or organ system while maintaining strong relevance to kidney disease and transplantation. The program may include investigator-initiated clinical or translational studies, collaborative laboratory programs, research cores, biorepositories, data resources, pilot funding mechanisms, and interdisciplinary partnerships spanning immunology, inflammation, tissue injury and repair, epithelial and endothelial biology, vascular biology, critical care, surgery, pathology, nephrology, transplantation, and basic science programs.
* Develops a pipeline of physician-scientists, translational investigators, and multidisciplinary research teams whose work bridges nephrology, transplantation, immunology, vascular biology, tissue injury and repair, and other cross-cutting domains by mentoring students, trainees, staff and faculty toward independent funding and scholarly productivity.

**Qualifications**

* D., M.D./Ph.D. or equivalent degree.
* Board certification or eligibility in nephrology or a closely related discipline is expected.
* Eligible for faculty appointment at professor rank in the Department of Medicine.
* Eligible for New York State medical licensure and credentialing at Westchester Medical Center.
* Eligible for appointment to the medical staff of WMC.
* Computer literacy in PC and Mac-based software applications including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and MS Office Suite; other software specific to research specialization, as needed.
* Established record as a senior academic physician-scientist or translational investigator in nephrology, transplantation, immunology, kidney injury/repair, epithelial or endothelial biology, or related fields.
* Demonstrated history of extramural funding, high-impact scholarship, program building, interdisciplinary collaboration, and mentorship of trainees and faculty required.
* Internationally or nationally recognized expertise in nephrology, transplantation biology, renal injury/repair, translational immunology, epithelial biology, endothelial biology, or related scientific domains.
* Demonstrated success securing extramural research support and leading productive, collaborative, and compliant research programs.
* Documented capacity to generate and sustain investigator-initiated funding from federal, foundation, industry, philanthropic, and endowment-related sources.
* Ability to prepare and execute a strategic plans addressing research, funding, recruitment, and sustainability plan with measurable milestones for grants, publications, mentorship, program development, and responsible use of endowed chair resources.
* Experience with donor stewardship, advancement partnerships, annual impact reporting, research compliance, grant administration, and transparent stewardship of restricted or endowed funds preferred.
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills with ability to engage faculty, trainees, hospital leadership, research administration, philanthropy, donors, industry partners, and external scientific collaborators.
* Strong leadership, mentoring, planning, and organizational skills in an academic health center environment.
* Ability to develop research infrastructure, recruit and retain research staff, manage start-up resources in alignment with institutional mission and endowed purpose.
* Commitment to education, mentorship, academic citizenship, research integrity, professionalism, inclusive and engaging work ethic and ethical conduct.
* Ability to work cooperatively within the academic health center as well as external partners.
* Academic health center; clinical patient-centered facilities, research labs, office, and teaching environments.
* Activities may include meetings, teaching sessions, clinical collaboration, laboratory/ research oversight, and occasional travel for scientific meetings.
* Standard academic health center, research, and clinical environments; must comply with institutional safety, biosafety, clinical, and research compliance requirements.

**Minimum Salary**
USD $350,000.00/Yr.
  
  
**Maximum Salary**
USD $400,000.00/Yr.

jobs.description:
The Department of Medicine and Section of Palliative Care in the Division of General Internal Medicine is seeking a full-time physician (MD/DO), PhD scientist or PharmD in a relevant field with a research focus on palliative care and serious illness at the levels of Assistant Professor, appointment or tenure stream, Associate Professor, appointment or tenure stream and Professor, appointment stream or tenured depending on qualifications and career track to serve as the Associate Chief of Research (ACR) and Director of the Palliative Research Center (PaRC). In this role, the ACR will collaborate closely with the Section Faculty and report directly to the Section Chief.
  
  
The Section of Palliative Care is a multidisciplinary team committed to improving quality of life for patients and families through delivery of quality palliative care, education of palliative care skills and advancement in palliative care innovation. We work with patients at academic hospitals and at outpatient clinics throughout the region. Our fellowship program is nationally recognized and comprised of four fellowship tracks to accommodate diverse career goals.
  
  
The Palliative Research Center (PaRC) consists of faculty from across the Schools of Health Sciences, including researchers from palliative care and many medical subdisciplines, nursing, and public health. PaRC supports researchers throughout their careers and encourages collaboration between faculty members across disciplines.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Research Leadership – Develop and implement the strategic research mission of the Section and the Palliative Research Center (PaRC).
* Recruitment and Mentorship – Recruit junior and mid-level investigators and provide mentorship for palliative care investigators.
* Collaboration and Engagement – Promote synergy and partnerships across disciplines and University departments, schools and institutes.
* Grant Funding – Nurture collaborative relationships with foundations and industries and advance federal research projects (NIH, PCORI).

**Resources Available**

* Palliative Research Center (PaRC)
* Center for Research on Health Care (CRHC)
* VA Center for Health Care Evaluation, Research Promotion (CHERP)
* Institute for Clinical Research Education (ICRE)

Applicants for Assistant Professor, appointment or tenure stream, should have three or more years of experience in the field of clinical and/or health services research; have achieved or established the ability to attain external research funding; have dispersed results through peer-reviewed publications and other scientific forums; have noteworthy teaching experience; and established the capability for continued career development, promotion, and tenure.
  
  
Applicants for Associate Professor, appointment or tenure stream, should have five or more years of experience in the field of clinical and/or health services research; have independent, external research funding and an extensive record of peer-reviewed publications; have substantial teaching experience; and demonstrate the ability for continued, impactful, independent scholarly contributions and leadership.
  
  
Applicants for Professor, appointment stream or tenured, will have served five to seven years as Associate Professor. The rank of professor regards the individual accomplishments of respected knowledge and status in a distinguished ﬁeld of learning and the achievement of successful teaching knowledge and practices. The professor should have obtained enhanced stature in their ﬁeld through contributions of scholarship, professional practice, and leadership in professional and learning organizations.
  
  
We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and a dynamic working environment.
  
  
Interested applicants should submit a curriculum vitae and apply to requisition number 26004568 via: https://www.join.pitt.edu.
  
  
The University of Pittsburgh is an equal opportunity employer/disability/veteran.
  
  
**About UPMC:**
The University of Pittsburgh and its partner, the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC), are committed to excellence in biomedical science and health care in southwestern Pennsylvania. Together, they focus on training the next generation of health care specialists, conducting groundbreaking research, and delivering outstanding patient care. The University encompasses six schools of health sciences, all sharing a mission to advance education, biomedical research, and health promotion. Notably, the University has doubled its NIH support since 1998 and is a leader in NIH-funded institutions, underscoring its commitment to research infrastructure and faculty recruitment.

jobs.description:
**Description**
Job Description Summary:
  
  
Samuel Merritt University graduates improve health outcomes and reduce disparities for all members of our communities. We have spent more than a century preparing outstanding healthcare professionals through immersive learning and community engagement, and are deeply committed to transforming healthcare through diversity and inclusion. At the School of Nursing, we are at the forefront of educational innovation in theory and practice to prepare highly competent professional nursing leaders who are engaged in the advancement of nursing practice and the improvement of health for diverse populations/peoples. Our mission is to prepare highly skilled nurse clinicians and nurse leaders who promote health and well-being across diverse populations and communities, recognize the importance of Social Determinants of Health, and practice with compassion, kindness, and respect.
  
  
Join a team of dedicated educators! Our faculty are known for their passion for growing the nursing vocation. With this passion, we strive to awaken curiosity in our students and instill lifelong learning. Congruent with our values, we work hard to inspire service and leadership in our students and in our surrounding communities. For this reason, the role of faculty is vitally important because of their unmatched position to shape the professional and personal development of graduates. Adjunct faculty are responsible for creating a positive learning environment for students in accordance with the educational objectives of the course and implement the policies identified in the course syllabus to ensure the successful achievement of course objectives.
  
  
There are multiple adjunct faculty (Theory, Lab, and Clinical) opportunities available for the Fresno campus. These opportunities are ideal for working nurses who are not seeking full-time teaching positions, but have expertise in disciplines of medical-surgical nursing, critical care, pediatrics, maternity, community health, mental health nursing or simulation and an interest in teaching and student mentorship.

Education & Experience

* Demonstrated current competence in theory or clinical area at the level of the student being taught.

* Function effectively independently and as a member of a team.

* Express and exchange ideas by means of the spoken word in person, or over the phone.
* Receive detailed information through verbal and written communication.
* Read and write clearly.
* Model appropriate ethical and professional behaviors.
* Embrace mission, vision, and values of the program, school of nursing, and university.

Regular

United States of America (Exempt)

Full time

**Organization**
At Samuel Merritt University (SMU), we are dedicated to fostering a supportive, inclusive community committed to advancing healthcare through exceptional education, compassionate care, and community service. Known for our leading-edge programs in health sciences, SMU equips students and faculty with the knowledge and skills to make impactful contributions to health and wellness.
  
  
We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. SMU welcomes applicants from all backgrounds and is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where anyone can thrive and reach their full potential.
  
  
Samuel Merritt University currently provides base salary ranges for all positions-on job advertisements-in the United States based on local requirements. Individual compensation will ultimately be determined based on a variety of relevant factors including but-not limited to qualifications, geographic location, and other relevant skills.
  
  
**Benefits**
Samuel Merritt University offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
  
  

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Mental health and wellness resources
* Education reimbursement
* Employee discounts through Marketplace

* Nine paid holidays, plus a paid holiday break between Christmas and New Year’s Day

Samuel Merritt University Has Been Made Aware Of Individuals Posing As SMU Recruiters, Particularly For Remote Positions. To Help Protect Yourself, Please Keep The Following In Mind

Please remain cautious and protect your personal information throughout your job search.

jobs.title: Professor in Social Consequences of AI in Organizational Communication
jobs.description:
Job #JPF03137

* Communication / College of Letters & Science - Social Sciences / UC Santa Barbara

### **Position overview**

**Position title:** Assistant, Associate, or Professor

**Salary range:** A reasonable estimate that the University expects to pay for this position at 100% time is $95,000 - $435,000 at the Assistant, Associate, or Professor Level.

**Percent time:** 100%

**Anticipated start:** July 1, 2027 or later

### **Application Window**

**Open date:** September 21, 2026

**Next review date:** Wednesday, Oct 21, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.

**Final date:** Wednesday, Mar 31, 2027 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled.

### **Position description**

The UCSB Department of Communication is recruiting for a tenure-track/tenured open rank faculty position.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming how humans communicate, coordinate, and organize across workplaces, institutions, and society. AI increasingly shapes organizational decision-making, collaboration, knowledge production, expertise, and identity while reconfiguring power, authority, accountability, and the boundaries between human and machine agency. These developments create new opportunities to revisit foundational organizational communication theories while also demanding new theoretical and empirical approaches to understanding AI as a sociotechnical actor embedded within organizational and institutional systems. We seek a scholar who conducts innovative, theoretically grounded, and empirically rigorous research using quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-method approaches that addresses the social consequences of AI from an organizational communication perspective. This could include, but is not limited to, topics such as human-AI collaboration; algorithmic decision-making and governance; sustainability; visibility and surveillance; ethics and corporate social responsibility; power and inequality; and (dis)empowerment of underrepresented groups. We are particularly interested in scholarship that advances organizational communication theory by examining how algorithms or algorithmic systems reshape communication processes, organizing practices, and institutional change, rather than only treating AI as a methodological or analytical tool. We anticipate that the faculty hire will make meaningful connections and engage in multidisciplinary endeavors across campus such as the Mellichamp Initiative in Mind & Machine Intelligence, the Department of Technology Management, the Center for Information Technology & Society’s research foci in AI, the Pahl Center for the Study of Critical Social Issues, and campus-wide initiatives in AI and related communities of practice.

UCSB is ranked among the top public universities in the United States, and the Department of Communication is also highly ranked in worldwide comparisons. UCSB is a designated Hispanic Serving Institution, and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution. It offers several programs to support incoming faculty, including housing assistance (Faculty Housing | Campus Housing) and various grant support programs.

### **Qualifications**

**Basic qualifications** (required at time of application)

Completed all requirements for a Ph.D. (or equivalent) in a Communication or related field except dissertation by the time of application.

**Additional qualifications** (required at time of start)

A Ph.D. (or equivalent) in communication or a related field by the time of appointment, with a desired start date of July 1, 2027 or later.

**Preferred qualifications**

* Demonstrated research excellence relevant to the job call in the form of research quality, productivity, and a unique scholarly contribution to the area of the social consequences of AI in organizational communication as well as to the communication discipline.

* Potential or demonstrated ability to contribute to the department’s organizational communication area.

* Potential or demonstrated ability to attract and supervise graduate students interested in organizational communication.

* Potential or demonstrated ability to teach organizational communication and potentially other coursework to undergraduate and graduate students.

* Potential or demonstrated commitments to student success and inclusive pedagogy.

* Potential or demonstrated ability to be a conscientious member of the department and university community member.

### **Application Requirements**

**Document requirements**

* Cover Letter - A cover letter that highlights your qualifications, research agenda, teaching capabilities, and service contributions
* Curriculum Vitae - Your most recently updated C.V.
* Evidence of Teaching Effectiveness - Please upload one (or more) student evaluations from a course you have instructed or assisted.
* Teaching Statement - Please upload a Teaching Statement which explains your teaching methodology.
* Research Sample #1 - Published or completed research.
* Research Sample #2 - Published or completed research.
* Research Sample #3 - Published or completed research.

**Reference requirements**

* 3-5 letters of reference required

Applicants should provide the names and contact information for at least 3 references and must request letters of reference within the system in order to complete application requirements.

**Apply link:** https://recruit.ap.ucsb.edu/JPF03137

**Help contact:** hyoder@ucsb.edu

### **About UC Santa Barbara**

As a condition of employment, the finalist will be required to disclose if they are subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct.

* “Misconduct” means any violation of the policies or laws governing conduct at the applicant’s previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies or laws prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment or discrimination as defined by the employer.

jobs.description:
**Overview:**

Mount Marty University, a Catholic, Benedictine liberal arts institution sponsored by the Sisters of Sacred Heart Monastery, invites applications for an open rank, tenure-track faculty position in Business with expertise in Marketing.

Located in Yankton, South Dakota, Mount Marty seeks a teacher-scholar or an accomplished practitioner who will serve as a primary faculty member for marketing within the Business program. Rank and salary will be commensurate with credentials and experience.

The successful candidate will demonstrate a primary commitment to undergraduate teaching, the ability to connect marketing theory to contemporary practice for a broad range of students, and sustained professional or scholarly activity that enriches classroom instruction.

Mount Marty welcomes applications from candidates early in their academic careers and from those moving into teaching from professional practice. New faculty are supported by the university’s Teaching and Learning Center, which provides mentoring, instructional design assistance, and ongoing development for colleagues new to the classroom. Review of applications begins immediately. Position is open until filled.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Teach the breadth of the marketing curriculum at the undergraduate level, including areas such as principles of marketing, consumer behavior, digital and social media marketing, and marketing research, along with foundational business courses required across the program, at a load of twelve credit hours per semester.
* Contribute to course offerings in adjacent areas such as Economics, Operations Management, Information Systems, and Human Resource Management as institutional need requires.
* Coordinate course scheduling with the Registrar’s Office and participate in ongoing program assessment.
* Provide academic advising to Business majors and support student professional development, internships, and career preparation.
* Work collaboratively with colleagues in the Business Department and across the university to support mission integration in the curriculum.
* Contribute actively to the intellectual and communal life of the university through departmental and institutional service.

**Qualifications:**

* **Education:** An earned doctorate in Business Administration, Marketing, or a closely related field is preferred by time of appointment. Candidates who are ABD will be considered provided all doctoral requirements are completed in the fall of 2027. Candidates holding a master’s degree in Business Administration or a related field together with substantial professional experience in marketing will also be given full consideration.
* **Commitment to Teaching:** Demonstrated effectiveness or clear promise as an undergraduate teacher, with the ability, or evident capacity to develop the ability, to make marketing concepts accessible and compelling to a diverse student body and to connect classroom learning to current practice.
* **Professional and Scholarly Activity:** Evidence of continuing scholarly work, professional practice, or applied engagement in the discipline appropriate to an undergraduate teaching institution.
* **Mission Alignment:** Commitment in principle and practice to Mount Marty University’s mission as a Catholic and Benedictine university rooted in the liberal arts.
* **Benedictine Charism:** Capacity to integrate Benedictine practices of hospitality, attentive listening, communal searching for truth, and the balance of work and prayer into teaching and academic citizenship.

**Work Authorization:**

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire without current or future employer sponsorship. Mount Marty University is not able to sponsor, petition for, provide supporting documentation for, or assume sponsorship of any employment-based visa or work authorization status at this time.

Employment is contingent upon satisfactory completion of a background check, verification of identity and unrestricted employment authorization as required by federal law, and the ability to be physically present on the Yankton campus by the position start date.

**Required Application Materials:**

Applicants must submit the following through the university’s online application system:

* A letter of application addressing the position’s requirements and responsibilities.
* A current curriculum vitae.
* A statement of teaching philosophy.
* A statement describing how your experience and commitments align with Mount Marty’s Catholic and Benedictine mission.
* Contact information for three professional references, at least one of whom can address teaching capability.

**About the University**

Located on a beautifully maintained 80-acre campus along the bluffs of the Missouri River, Mount Marty’s hallmark is outstanding teaching, small class size, and a strong commitment to the liberal arts in the Catholic Benedictine tradition. The campus is minutes away from Lewis and Clark Lake, one of South Dakota’s most popular recreation areas, and is within driving distance of the Twin Cities, Kansas City, and Omaha.

Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. For more information about Mount Marty University and its mission, please visit www.mountmarty.edu. Mount Marty University is an affirmative action, equal opportunity employer. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure or Non-Tenure Faculty - Veterinary Anesthesia Educator, Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
jobs.description:
Clemson University: Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
  
  
Location
  
  
CVM - COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE HUB(001184) BLDG001184
  
  
Open Date
  
  
Jul 22, 2026
  
  
**Description**
The Clemson University Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine (PCVM) is seeking applicants for a full-time or part-time position to serve as a Veterinary Anesthesia Educator. This faculty position will play a pivotal role in the development and implementation of the Clemson DVM curriculum. The successful candidate will have a primary instructional role developing and delivering anesthesia didactic curriculum, clinical skills, and perioperative care in the integrated Clemson DVM curriculum. This role is designed to attract outstanding educators and experienced clinicians who are enthusiastic about teaching anesthesia skills and knowledge. Board certification is encouraged but not required.
  
  
The Clemson DVM curriculum https://www.clemson.edu/veterinary-medicine/students/curriculum.html is based upon integrative, collaborative team teaching where faculty with varying backgrounds can work together to offer students an inclusive and innovative learning environment. The Veterinary Anesthesia Educator will contribute to vertical and horizontal integration of the delivery of anesthesia principle concepts, including equipment, anesthetic drugs, protocol planning, pain management, and management of anesthetic complications using simulation and laboratory experiences. Utilizing state of the art classrooms, laboratories, and teaching technology with both live animals and simulation models, this faculty member will be asked to adopt an integrated educational approach to provide students with a strong foundation of cognitive, clinical, and professional competencies, in preparation for entry into the partially distributive model of clinical training in the fourth year.
  
  
While the PCVM will not have a specialty referral hospital, we will have a fully staffed community practice as well as a robust shelter medicine / spay-neuter program. The Veterinary Anesthesia Educator will work closely with the community practice and shelter medicine clinicians to integrate classroom concepts that translate seamlessly into real world experiences. A clinical service commitment is not required; however, interested individuals could engage in teaching activities in our community practice. Additionally, this faculty member will engage in scholarly activities, which can include curriculum development, programmatic or curricular assessment, scholarship of teaching and learning, and other similar activities.
  
  
Finally, we will consider a hybrid academic appointment for a board-certified anesthesiologist. If desired, this individual may seek a combination of a part-time academic appointment at Clemson while also having a part-time position in private referral practice. The possibility of a 9-month or 12-month contract are options that can be discussed with the department chair.
  
  
**Overview Of The Position**
Reporting to the Department Chair and working closely with the Foundational Sciences and Clinical Skills Leads, the Veterinary Anesthesia Educator will:
  
  

* Create and deliver the anesthesia course in year 2 and participate in other clinically based, team-taught courses in the curriculum including activities in the Clinical Skills surgery lab.
* Assist in the development and delivery of the anesthesia rotation in the clinical year curriculum.
* Provide consultation services for cases seen by Clemson PCVM Veterinary Services.
* Aid in development of the Clemson PCVM lab and clinical case policies and procedures.
* Develop assessment strategies in alignment with the overall competency-based curriculum.
* Collaborate with other faculty members to ensure integration of knowledge and skills across years and courses
* Actively and effectively engage in student-centered instruction, coaching, and mentorship.
* Serve on PCVM and campus committees as appointed or elected.

**Additionally, The Faculty Member Must Have The Ability To**

* Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team, possess exemplary verbal and written communication skills, with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and function independently with limited supervision and guidance.
* Work in partnership with faculty and staff across multiple disciplines and functions across the college and university
* Participate in research and scholarship initiatives designed to improve educational and professional outcomes.

**Overview Of Clemson And The PCVM**
Located in South Carolina’s beautiful and fast-growing Upstate, Clemson University is the land-grant university of South Carolina and ranks among the country’s top 50 national public universities in the U.S. News & World Report. The University has nearly 23,400 students (including nearly 18,600 undergraduates) who can select from 80 undergraduate and 110 graduate degree programs. Clemson employs over 1,150 full-time faculty and has an annual budget expenditure of over $900M. Clemson University maintains its status as an R1 Carnegie Research Institution while maintaining a strong focus on undergraduate education.
  
  
The PCVM is currently seeking accreditation by the American Veterinary Medicine Association-Council on Education to offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree to approximately 80 students per cohort starting in 2026 (pending approval). The PCVM plans to utilize a partial distributive model of clinical training for students. Its brand-new state of the art campus will reside in Pendleton, SC, near the T. Ed Garrison Arena, will house research and teaching labs, and utilize both ambulatory services as well as teaching sites at the Clemson University Equine Center, Lamaster Dairy Cattle Center, and other locations for education in the field.
  
  
In 2023, the Board of Trustees approved Clemson Elevate, the university’s new strategic plan. Clemson Elevate is built on 3 pillars: deliver the #1 student experience, double research by 2035, and transform lives statewide and beyond. The PCVM was named as a strategic priority for the university, demonstrating the importance of the new college to the future of the university and the state. We are excited to attract a team of top talent as we build the new college.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Minimum qualifications include:**

* DVM or equivalent with 3 plus years of relevant experience.
* Applicants must demonstrate a solid foundation in veterinary anesthesia and the ability to teach anesthesia skills to veterinary students in classroom, laboratory, and clinical settings.
* Commitment to excellence and creativity in education.
* Licensed or eligible for licensure to practice veterinary medicine in South Carolina and ability to obtain a DEA license.

**Preferred Qualifications Include**

* 5 plus years of relevant experience in veterinary medicine or education
* Experience in anesthesia skills education, simulation pedagogy, and/or competency-based assessment
* Demonstrated experience mentoring learners (students, interns, residents, or technicians)
* Board certification or residency training in a veterinary specialty recognized by the ABVS (ACVAA, ECVAA, etc.)
